- The chapter opens on **Sadzu Du, Dzego** in the year 3724 Firemoon 10, establishing time and place. [c14-b1]  
- Zei’s alarm buzzes, prompting him to rise, order a fruit‑vegetable juice via the room‑service menu, and dress. [c14-b2] [c14-b3] [c14-b4]  
- After drinking the juice, Zei leaves his room, heads to the lobby, and notices someone waving. [c14-b5] [c14-b6]  
- The wave comes from Bai, who joins Zei at a table in the lobby restaurant. [c14-b7] [c14-b8]  
- Bai teases the restaurant robots with a cute phrase and asks how Zei has been. [c14-b9] [c14-b10]  
- Bai probes Zei about his knowledge of other players’ strategies, noting the upcoming semi‑final. [c14-b12] [c14-b13]  
- Zei questions whether Bai has obtained information illicitly; Bai reassures him he is merely a social observer. [c14-b15] [c14-b16]  
- Zei acknowledges the need for basic social skills to survive, and thanks Bai for his help. [c14-b18] [c14-b19]  
- Zei asks for concrete advice; Bai warns that all opponents, especially Gun, are overly impatient and rush their moves. [c14-b22] [c14-b23]  
- Zei accepts the counsel, nodding that he will avoid unnecessary haste. [c14-b25] [c14-b26]  
- A robot delivers Bai’s vegetable‑rice dish and tea; Zei orders his own tea and watches. [c14-b27]  
- Zei’s watch buzzes; a car arrives to transport him to the semi‑final arena. [c14-b28]  
- The announcer declares the semi‑finals, recaps forty days of qualifying matches, and lists the top four qualifiers, including Zei (Pafogai Du) and Gun (Dzundei). [c14-b30] [c14-b31]  
- The semi‑final match will pit Zei against Gun, with a new rule: intervention‑turn resources are cut by eighty percent and five shrines are added that XOR their contents each thousand turns. [c14-b32] [c14-b33]  
- Zei instantly grasps that the shrines break mass conservation; XOR is reversible, so the board will become increasingly cluttered, making intervention turns about steering rather than building. [c14-b35]  
- He prepares his usual walls, gliders, and spaceships, but also equips a newly designed symbol‑carrying spaceship that can change direction with minimal intervention. [c14-b36]  
- Zei plans to position his ships so that after two intervention turns they pass the shrines, creating an eternal glider factory that repeatedly spawns gliders. [c14-b38]  
- He sacrifices the western sector, focusing glider storms to protect his central, eastern, and southern advances. [c14-b40]  
- As the match begins, Zei continuously optimizes his structures until the first intervention turn arrives, when he launches gliders to convert rock into symbols and factories. [c14-b42] [c14-b45]  
- He realizes his weakness: building a new symbol‑carrying ship requires four intervention turns, leaving him with only three such ships to defend. [c14-b46]  
- Just before the second intervention turn, Zei’s ship and two of Gun’s ships cross in the centre, revealing Gun’s aggressive intent. [c14-b47] [c14-b48]  
- Zei chooses to send gliders that will bounce between the centre shrine and the south/east shrines; Gun mirrors this strategy with his own ships. [c14-b49] [c14-b50]  
- The audience can see the full board, though Zei and Gun have limited views. [c14-b51]  
- A few hundred turns later, Gun’s glider factories prove more effective, destroying one of Zei’s symbol‑carrying ships and setting up a collision course between their remaining ships. [c14-b53] [c14-b54]  
- Zei is left with a single mobile ship in the east; he hides it near the northeastern base and plans a covert glider strike on Gun’s symbols via the northern shrine. [c14-b55] [c14-b56]  
- As the fourth intervention turn passes, Gun enjoys a material advantage, while Zei’s only strength is concealment. [c14-b61] [c14-b62]  
- Zei begins a five‑turn construction of a new symbol‑carrying ship, simultaneously replicating a rock pattern that will spawn an eternal factory between the centre and north shrines. [c14-b63] [c14-b64]  
- By the fifth turn his hidden factory damages Gun’s north‑west bases, though Zei cannot measure the impact. [c14-b64]  
- Soon after, Gun’s remaining ship moves northward, Zei’s last southeast symbol is erased by glider storms, and Zei creates another factory along the western centre line. [c14-b65] [c14-b66]  
- Zei must remain stationary for three thousand turns while his new ship is built, becoming a sitting duck. [c14-b67]  
- The sixth intervention turn lets Gun’s ship survive a glider barrage, but it is later destroyed after entering Zei’s visual range. [c14-b69] [c14-b70]  
- Zei calculates that Gun could see his old ship but not the one under construction, prompting him to reinforce walls on the west and diagonal while ignoring the south, trusting existing debris as protection. [c14-b71] [c14-b72]  
- During the seventh turn Zei pours all resources into finishing the new ship; the next turn will allow a steering command. [c14-b73]  
- A massive glider storm assaults Zei’s position; walls hold briefly before the gliders breach them. [c14-b74] [c14-b75]  
- The eighth turn arrives just in time for Zei to complete his new ship and issue a final command: both ships will head west, using the wreck of the old ship to trigger a glider storm at the northern shrine. [c14-b76] [c14-b77]  
- At the ninth turn Zei bounces a glider off a near‑destroyed rock formation to re‑adjust eternal factories, hoping to render previously safe zones hazardous, and launches an additional westward glider attack. [c14-b78]  
- The tenth turn yields only debris, while the eleventh turn sees Zei devise a complex bounce‑off‑wall tactic that creates alternating glider streams between centre, north, and western shrines, mirrored eastward. [c14-b79] [c14-b81] [c14-b83]  
- By the twelfth turn offense becomes impossible amid overwhelming debris; Zei focuses on building defensive walls. [c14-b84]  
- The thirteenth turn shows Zei’s four‑layer wall fortress beginning to crumble faster than he can repair it. [c14-b85]  
- Finally, an alarm sounds announcing Zei Leimin as the winner of the semi‑finals; he exhales in relief. [c14-b86] [c14-b87] [c14-b88]  
- In the waiting room Zei watches the final between Deluin (Redshire) and Kau (Geijaken); Deluin’s patient wall‑building outlasts Kau’s limited factories. [c14-b90] [c14-b91] [c14-b92]  
- Seven thousand turns later Kau hides behind the southern shrine, but three thousand more turns of glider debris force his defeat, and Deluin is declared champion after ten‑thousand‑two‑hundred turns. [c14-b93] [c14-b94]  
- After the match Deluin exits the elevator, compliments Zei’s style, and suggests they have tea together. [c14-b95] [c14-b96] [c14-b97] [c14-b98] [c14-b99] [c14-b100]  
- A robot greets them with the familiar phrase “jie mo kai tu jie hei ja ma?” and a menu appears, prompting Zei’s astonishment. [c14-b105] [c14-b106] [c14-b107] [c14-b109]  
- Zei and Deluin discuss the new symbols being A/B‑tested for Dzegoban version nine, speculating on pronunciation markers. [c14-b110] [c14-b111] [c14-b112] [c14-b113] [c14-b114] [c14-b115] [c14-b116] [c14-b117] [c14-b118]  
- Deluin explains that Dzegoban has only 256 roots, can be learned in under a month, and blends visual hieroglyphs with mathematically‑styled grammar. [c14-b118]  
- He invites Zei to visit Redshire for tutoring; Zei declines due to lack of funds, but Deluin shows pictures of Redshire’s castles, pine forests, snowy mountains, and an icy waterfall. [c14-b119] [c14-b120] [c14-b121] [c14-b122] [c14-b123] [c14-b124]  
- Deluin reflects that praising a country’s natural beauty is not a backhanded insult, because human effort maintains both nature and infrastructure. [c14-b125] [c14-b126]  
- He jokes that he will use his championship winnings to fund Zei’s trip, hoping it can happen within fifteen days. [c14-b127] [c14-b128] [c14-b129] [c14-b130]

- The chapter opens in Freetown, United Cities on 3724 Firemoon 17, establishing the setting. [c15-b1]

- Zei pleads not to win the trophy under these circumstances, showing his moral conflict. [c15-b86]  
- Su directs Zei to meet Den in the southern mountain pyramid, hinting at a possible assignment in Pafogai. [c15-b87] [c15-b88]  
- Zei arrives at a new entrance to the mountain pyramid, uses his watch to unlock a green‑circle door, and enters Den’s chamber. [c15-b90] [c15-b93] [c15-b94]  
- Den thanks Zei for coming and tells him he is one of the few capable of helping Dzego survive the coming year. [c15-b96] [c15-b98]

- The chapter follows Keeper Gladias on a day in Meldan, Veridia, dated 3724 Fruitmoon 11. [c17-b0] [c17-b1]  
- Gladias walks along a tree‑lined path to the circular Veridian Parliament building. [c17-b2]

- The chapter follows Gladias and Zei, two Veridian visitors inside a cafeteria deep within the mountain pyramid, dated 3724 Grapetime 15. [c19-b1] [c19-b2]  
- They discuss meeting Den, a High Council member of the Kungaupei who runs the institution defending against the Arctic shadow campaign for a decade, and whom Veridia wants to learn from instead of its own government. [c19-b4]  
- A swarm of small drones enters, triggering alerts on Gladias’s watch; the watch flags them as threats because its language database is outdated. [c19-b5] [c19-b6]  
- Zei checks his own watch, decodes the interface, and discovers that “kun gau” means Kungaupei security robots, confirming the drones’ purpose. [c19-b14] [c19-b20] [c19-b23]  
- The watches also display real‑time air quality data (CO₂ and PM2.5), reflecting Veridia’s cultural emphasis on clean air and pandemic prevention. [c19-b37] [c19-b40] [c19-b42]  
- A robot serves a salad‑tea combo to Gladias and a mushroom‑rice‑tea combo to Zei; Gladias identifies the dish as “Number Ten” from Dzego food trucks and they swap plates, noting the food is superior to Veridian fare. [c19-b46] [c19-b48] [c19-b52]  
- Zei’s watch receives a cryptic, zip‑coin‑paid message from the Beautiful Plants food court in Sadzu Du, addressed to him, containing links to over sixty gigabytes of data and demanding an 80 % download. [c19-b55] [c19-b61] [c19-b68]  
- The two decide to walk to the mountain’s internal digital‑archive node, exiting the cafeteria and navigating tunnels to a large ornamented door adorned with whimsical animal illustrations and a slogan translating to “Outside of a dog, a book is man’s best friend; inside of a dog, it’s too dark to read.” [c19-b73] [c19-b78] [c19-b81]  
- Inside the grand library, shelves form a three‑way book maze; terminals line the open area, and a robed librarian greets them, questioning their purpose. [c19-b82] [c19-b86] [c19-b88]  
- Zei explains he seeks the “very large files” from the archive; the librarian, amused, assists by connecting a data cable, initiating a rapid download that reaches 100 % in eight minutes. [c19-b95] [c19-b101] [c19-b102]  
- Robots deliver tea in differing cup styles, highlighting subtle cultural preferences. [c19-b104] [c19-b110]  
- Gladias browses a Dzego architecture book, noting the evolution from utilitarian post‑war designs to later lavish underground rooms with imitation windows or plant‑filled interiors. [c19-b111] [c19-b112]  
- The download script then asks “What did you do on Firemoon 10th?” Zei postpones his meeting with Den, fearing the task is complex, and runs the query in a sandboxed, journaling file system to avoid privacy leaks. [c19-b116] [c19-b119] [c19-b122]  
- Zei’s device reconstructs his personal log of Firemoon 10th: his last Minpentai semifinal, meetings with Bai and Deluin, a courtyard visit at the same cafeteria address, and detailed recollections of Deluin’s invitation to Redshire and philosophical remarks. [c19-b124] [c19-b126] [c19-b135]  
- He sends this exhaustive narrative back to the archive, triggering analysis that reveals the data bundle comprises recent movies, health records, and AI‑generated Arctic sermons, encoded via a five‑of‑six erasure code and level‑two obfuscation using steganographic language‑model weights. [c19-b144] [c19-b148] [c19-b151]  
- The final decoded message, authored by Deluin, apologizes for a month of silence, explains that the Arctic Empire recently seized Redshire’s devices, back‑doored them, and that Deluin, whose parents cooperate with the Arctics, is being forced to travel to the Empire’s core, hoping to aid Zei later but fearing this may be their last contact. [c19-b152] [c19-b153]  
- World details emerging: the Kungaupei High Council’s security robots, zipcoin‑based anonymous messaging, Veridian environmental watch sensors, the mountain‑pyramid library’s physical‑digital hybrid archive, sandboxed hand‑device execution, and the Arctic Empire’s surveillance and device‑reclamation program. [c19-b4] [c19-b7] [c19-b40] [c19-b82] [c19-b122] [c19-b152]

- Mov criticizes society’s complacency, noting that even Silverchat has become indifferent to maintaining Veridia’s infrastructure [c20-b33]  
- He notes that the Keepers were split into three isolated groups, preventing coordinated action against Delwart [c20-b35]  
- Mov has placed trackers on two Keepers but has not yet exposed them, preferring to keep surveillance options open [c20-b39] [c20-b40]  
- Seila wants to act for Febric and Hreda but feels powerless; she decides to investigate the Order instead [c20-b44] [c20-b46]  
- Mov warns against using a personal copter, fearing it would attract Arctic attention [c20-b48]  
- Seila and Mov don privacy robes, hail a taxi, and cryptographically approve payment by tapping a green circle on the door [c20-b50] [c20-b51]

- Inside, Mov removes his hood to appear less threatening; Seila does the same before the door is opened [c20-b60] [c20-b61]  
- The resident introduces himself as Telroy, a Keeper in the cybersecurity rubric group, and agrees to discuss the Order and Delwart [c20-b63] [c20-b67]  
- Telroy confirms Delwart’s anti‑war stance, his belief that military matters are zero‑sum, and his push for delayed public‑safety data access to prevent insider trading [c20-b72] [c20-b73] [c20-b76]  
- Seila learns that Delwart also opposes tax breaks for open‑source military hardware, arguing such exemptions are immoral [c20-b81]  
- Telroy is surprised to hear that Delwart worked for Silverchat, a group he thought would champion openness [c20-b84] [c20-b85]  
- After leaving Telroy, Seila and Mov walk through a forested path to a mostly underground stone house, noting its low tax footprint and aesthetic design [c20-b87] [c20-b89]  
- They knock, a female voice asks “Who is this?”; Seila introduces herself and is invited in by Balme, the house’s occupant [c20-b91] [c20-b95]  
- Balme acknowledges the dire situation in Veridia and agrees to discuss Delwart’s views on education and freedom, emphasizing minimal state interference in schools [c20-b101] [c20-b104]  
- Seila contrasts Balme’s description of Delwart (pro‑freedom, anti‑Order) with Mov’s account (anti‑war, tax‑rubric opposition) [c20-b109] [c20-b110]

- Seila asks Balme to forward a message to Keepers working on social‑media openness rubrics; Balme consents, citing Keeper tradition of only discussing completed work [c20-b119] [c20-b123]  
- Seila later visits another house, burns 50 zipcoins as a signal of seriousness, and receives a matching notification on her watch [c20-b131] [c20-b132]  
- The resident, Lectoby, reveals his wife is trapped in Northglade and shares his own frustration with the Arctic invasion and the lack of decisive action from the Senate [c20-b140] [c20-b160]  
- Lectoby confirms he has not seen any strange contacts among his social‑media rubric peers, though his husband and Balme have experienced inconsistent anti‑war stances [c20-b152] [c20-b155]  
- Over tea, Lectoby speculates that Silverchat should care deeply about social‑media openness, yet no such activity is evident, suggesting a possible coincidence or hidden motive [c20-b166] [c20-b172]  
- Seila concludes, after gathering conflicting testimonies, that Delwart cannot be a Silverchat operative and states this explicitly before leaving [c20-b179]

- The chapter follows Jahn, an economist traveling through Freetown in a taxi, set in United Cities on 3724 Mistime 22. [c22-b0] [c22-b1] [c22-b2]  
- Freetown’s skyline mixes glass, steel, concrete, and stone, with chaotic streets and occasional public‑goods projects like a park‑projector. [c22-b2] [c22-b3]  
- Jahn notices lower street activity than usual and a series of advertisements for underground shelters priced from 50,000 to 325,000 zipcoins. [c22-b4] [c22-b6] [c22-b8]  
- He observes a surge in road construction, especially on the northern side, over the past six months. [c22-b9]  
- The taxi’s fare display shows unusually high congestion charges despite lighter traffic, prompting Jahn to ask the driver about the fees. [c22-b10] [c22-b14] [c22-b15]  
- The driver explains that taxes and tolls are being raised to fund defense, and hints at a possible link between shelter ownership and road projects. [c22-b15] [c22-b22]  
- Jahn shares gossip that defense companies, after annexing Redshire, formed a cartel, sold shelter space, and used proceeds to upgrade armor and weapons. [c22-b20] [c22-b21]  
- The driver suspects the government rewards private property used for public good by building roads that ease access to those shelters, a workaround of the maximum‑budget rule. [c22-b22] [c22-b23]  
- He warns that refusal to cooperate could lead to road closures, though air travel remains an option. [c22-b23]  
- The driver mentions Greater Plum Harbor’s reluctance to fund anti‑Arctic projects, fearing its Northglade node might be shut down. [c22-b24]  
- Jahn’s taxi stops at the Freetown Economics Institute, where he exits the vehicle. [c22-b26] [c22-b27] [c22-b29]  
- Inside the institute’s restaurant, Jahn meets Utaku, a fellow economist whose parents consider Freetown safer because of its defense focus. [c22-b32] [c22-b33] [c22-b34]  
- Utaku expresses cautious optimism about a proposed unified defense grid but doubts its substantive impact. [c22-b36] [c22-b37]  
- He notes that corporate insurance premiums on property have risen sharply after Redshire and Northglade annexations, then fell when defense packages were announced. [c22-b38] [c22-b39]  
- Utaku cites Dzego’s rapid adoption of privacy, bio‑safety, and indoor‑CO₂ standards, driven by a machinery originally meant for language upgrades. [c22-b40] [c22-b41]  
- Their dialogue turns to the early United Cities history, wars with the Arctics, and the co‑governance system that allocated parliamentary votes to neighboring cities. [c22-b44] [c22-b49]  
- They also discuss a past subsidy program that encouraged citizens to swap homes and citizenships, preserving cultural diversity. [c22-b50]  
- Freetown’s current constitution limits government taxation and regulation, offering subsidies to those whose personality‑test results match a “compatible” profile. [c22-b51]  
- Utaku contrasts this with Arturia’s merit‑based, university‑like society that pushes dissenters toward Freetown. [c22-b53] [c22-b54]  
- Both agree that voluntary ideological buy‑in, not genetics, underpins Freetown’s “freedom” ethos, requiring deep education to understand market‑based allocation of private property. [c22-b58] [c22-b59] [c22-b60]  
- Jahn orders a vegetable dish and tea, then creates a spreadsheet scoring possible defense‑funding options by revenue, collateral damage, and impact on freedom. [c22-b67]  
- Zei from Dzego calls, thanking Jahn for connecting her with the institute director and promising updates on defense activities. [c22-b68] [c22-b71] [c22-b72]  
- Zei reveals that Dzego, with defense‑company help, is hunting Arctic drones in Redshire, using a “kill chain” of jamming and attack drones. [c22-b75] [c22-b77] [c22-b83]  
- Jahn receives a view‑once file showing a hexagonal formation of seven jamming drones awaiting an Arctic ground drone. [c22-b79] [c22-b82] [c22-b84]  
- Subsequent view‑once files display the drones jamming, striking the target’s antenna and legs, and two “triangle” drones performing evasive “dance” maneuvers to survive. [c22-b92] [c22-b95] [c22-b101] [c22-b103]  
- Zei explains the strategy: use Arctic drones as practice for survival, then let the hexagon finish the kill and erase the drone’s data to deny the Arctics training material. [c22-b104] [c22-b105] [c22-b110]  
- An unexpected Arctic reinforcement forces the jammers to feign death, lure attackers, reform a circle, and attempt a final kill. [c22-b108] [c22-b109] [c22-b110]  
- The connection drops; Zei reports only one undamaged drone remains, tasked with chip‑and‑memory killing nearby drones before more Arctic units arrive. [c22-b119] [c22-b129] [c22-b131]  
- Zei describes their covert internet link to Redshire: steganographic audio embedded in voice/video calls, using error‑correcting codes to hide encrypted data from Arctics’ surveillance. [c22-b134] [c22-b136]  
- Their next major project is to capture an Arctic drone for analysis in Dzego, and Zei asks Jahn for assistance. [c22-b138] [c22-b140]

- The chapter follows Gladias and Zei in an enclosed room where a tabletop doubles as a digital screen showing four piles of circles, set on 3724 Frostime 1【c25-b1】【c25-b2】  
- Gladias is a novice player lacking strategic insight, eager to learn the game by playing【c25-b7】  
- Zei is the experienced mentor who explains the rules, the childhood origin of the game, and later reveals a winning algorithm【c25-b5】【c25-b22】【c25-b24】  
- The game’s rule: on a turn a player must take at least one circle from a single pile; the player who takes the last circle wins【c25-b5】【c25-b6】  
- Gladias makes his first move by tapping one circle in the top‑left pile【c25-b8】  
- Zei replies by tapping the top circle of the bottom‑right pile【c25-b10】  
- Gladias then takes three circles from the bottom‑left pile; Zei removes all but one circle from the bottom‑right pile【c25-b12】【c25-b14】  
- Gladias clears the remaining circles in the bottom‑left pile; Zei taps one circle in the top‑right pile【c25-b16】  
- Gladias clears the top‑left pile; Zei removes two of the three remaining circles in the top‑right pile【c25-b17】  
- Realising he cannot avoid leaving a single circle for Zei, Gladias admits defeat【c25-b19】【c25-b20】  
- Zei praises Gladias’s play and notes the game was common in childhood before technologies like Minpentai【c25-b21】【c25-b22】  
- Gladias asks for the “secret sauce”; Zei says it is a simple mental‑math algorithm that guarantees a win if the player can choose turn order【c25-b23】【c25-b24】  
- Zei defines the “secret sauce” as taking the XOR of the circle counts of each pile and aiming to keep the XOR sum zero after his moves【c25-b26】【c25-b36】  
- Using the initial counts 3, 4, 10, 13, Zei shows their binary forms, aligns them, and demonstrates that the column‑wise XOR is zero【c25-b28】【c25-b31】【c25-b34】【c25-b36】  
- After Gladias’s first move (3→2), the XOR becomes 1; Zei then reduces the last pile (13→12) restoring XOR zero【c25-b38】【c25-b40】【c25-b42】【c25-b45】【c25-b47】  
- Zei explains that any move from a zero XOR makes it non‑zero, but he can always choose a move that flips the highest‑order 1 back to zero, guaranteeing the winning position【c25-b48】【c25-b50】【c25-b52】  
- He adds that if the initial XOR is non‑zero, the first player can force a win; if it is zero, the second player is guaranteed victory【c25-b53】  
- Gladias reflects that he has never seen a game favor the second player, prompting Zei to note that such games are actually common when the starting XOR is zero【c25-b56】【c25-b57】  
- Zei argues the fundamental advantage of the second player is knowledge of the opponent’s move, allowing an exact counter‑move【c25-b59】【c25-b63】【c25-b65】  
- Zei describes three layers of the game: irreversible removal, reversible XOR balance, and the irreversible fact that it is the opponent’s turn when the XOR is balanced【c25-b72】  
- Signalling the end of the warm‑up, Zei asks whether the conflict over Veridia is a first‑player‑ or second‑player‑favoring game【c25-b73】【c25-b74】  
- He outlines the Arctics’ first‑move advantage: establishing spying infrastructure, pressuring officials, and attacking Redshire and Northglade【c25-b77】  
- Zei claims the battlefield advantage is technological, but the institutional struggle can be won by a counter‑strategy that aligns with the interests of Veridian actors【c25-b79】  
- He defines the needed tactic as “convincing” – showing people a course of action that already serves their own interests【c25-b80】【c25-b82】  
- Gladias proposes targeting the Courts, mirroring Delwart’s influence on the Order, to secure a decisive institutional move【c25-b86】【c25-b88】  
- Zei explains their advantage: they can tell the truth, which is self‑consistent, unlike the lies Delwart had to craft, making their influence campaign more reliable【c25-b90】【c25-b91】  
- Gladias initiates a secure call to Senator Verdow, using his watch to send a timed request【c25-b96】【c25-b97】  
- Verdow answers warmly, prompting Gladias to present the idea of influencing judges to counter the Arctics【c25-b99】【c25-b100】【c25-b102】  
- Zei interjects, reporting that their camera update has exposed backdoors, identified over a dozen judges, and that they have already neutralised some Arctics’ backdoors, giving them a strong foothold【c25-b104】  
- Verdow, impressed, proposes a radical legal plan: invoke the fourteenth Ground Law, declare the military lawbreakers, and empower the Courts to dismiss both the military and, if necessary, the Parliament【c25-b110】【c25-b111】【c25-b112】  
- He argues that such a sweeping judgement, though unprecedented, is precisely what Veridia needs in this crisis, and outlines a covert strategy to convince judges and the public before the Arctics can react【c25-b118】【c25-b119】  
- Zei affirms that Verdow’s plan is preferable to the low‑success alternatives of “trying harder” or surrendering【c25-b120】【c25-b121】

- The chapter takes place in Meldan, Veridia on Frostime 15, 3724, establishing the setting and date. [c28-b1]

- The chapter follows Zei’s night‑long command in Elenar Forest, Veridia, dated 3725 Snowmoon 30. [c30-b1]

- Lektor is the field commander who implements Zei’s slow‑retreat strategy. [c30-b2]  
- Deluin is a distant contact who sends encrypted messages to Zei. [c30-b3]  
- Bai, Fin, Emerald, Mu and other team members receive Zei’s forwarded intel. [c30-b5] [c30-b10]  
- Fin is a technical specialist who quickly evaluates the simulation‑access proposal. [c30-b6] [c30-b9]  
- Emerald is an AI that creates a real‑time chat group for collaborative hacking. [c30-b10] [c30-b11]  
- Mu is a field operator tasked later with exploiting southern‑front coordinates. [c30-b65] [c30-b71]  
- The Arctic drone fleet is the enemy, equipped with AI that detects incoming drones. [c30-b2] [c30-b19]  
- Zei’s goal is to delay Arctic detection long enough to survive until sunrise. [c30-b2] [c30-b19]  
- He fears the Arctic AI will adapt quickly and overwhelm Veridian forces. [c30-b19] [c30-b54]  
- Deluin admits Zei cannot trust him yet but offers proxy endpoints for safe queries. [c30-b4] [c30-b29]  
- The team plans to use simulated Arctic models to craft paper‑printed attack patterns. [c30-b11] [c30-b12]  
- Their method: iteratively modify patterns, measure detection time, keep improvements. [c30-b12]  
- They also intend to run gradient‑descent attacks on their own copy of the model to predict Arctic responses. [c30-b13]  
- Zei asks how fast the code can be ready; Emerald estimates ten minutes to code, a “longhour” to train. [c30-b14] [c30-b15]  
- The plan is to have the patterns printed and applied to drones just after sunrise. [c30-b17] [c30-b34]  
- After fifteen minutes, Bansunpei researchers report early success: detection time up 5 %, then 11 %. [c30-b21] [c30-b24] [c30-b26]  
- They add dummy queries to hide their activity from Arctic sentries. [c30-b29]  
- Night‑time simulations confirm the optimized patterns double detection time, then double again. [c30-b32] [c30-b33]  
- Lektor orders printing infrastructure two kilometres behind the line for safe retreat. [c30-b34]  
- Human Veridian soldiers move forward to apply the paper patterns, exploiting AI’s manual‑dexterity weakness. [c30-b35]

- Zei confirms the patterns are ready and authorizes shipment. [c30-b38] [c30-b39]  
- All non‑forward drones in North, Center, South and Naval groups report being equipped. [c30-b42] [c30-b45]

- Zei feels genuine joy, recalling Den’s earlier advice about unconventional tactics. [c30-b50] [c30-b51]

31.text:
- The chapter is set in Northglade, Veridia on the date 3725 Rainmoon 2. [c31-b1]  
- Zei, Bai and Mu climb a snow‑covered mountain staircase that is kept clear by a maintenance drone. [c31-b2]  
- At the summit they reach a circular platform offering a full view of the island of Northglade. [c31-b3‑c31-b4]  
- From the east they see the main city of Northglade; from the west and north they see endless snowy hills and a forested path. [c31-b4‑c31-b5]  
- A young man in a sweater and hood, Deluin, appears climbing the opposite staircase and greets Zei with a hug. [c31-b5‑c31-b9]  
- Deluin recognizes Bai from watching practice games in Sadzu Du and meets Mu, who distinguishes herself from Su of Dzego. [c31-b12‑c31-b16]  
- Deluin asks what happened; Zei begins recounting the Arctic occupation of Redshire. [c31-b17‑c31-b22]  
- Zei’s parents initially favored peace with the Arctic but became ardent supporters after the invasion, reflecting a broader Redshire shift. [c31-b22‑c31-b23]  
- The Arctic offered Redshire elites positions in Glasscrown to oversee integration of conquered peoples. [c31-b23‑c31-b24]  
- Zei “went native,” pretending to support the Arctic and leveraging her parents’ reputation and her Minpentai champion title. [c31-b24‑c31-b30]  
- The Minpentai tournament, originally a sport, was discovered by the Arctic to be effective training for modern warfare. [c31-b30‑c31-b34]  
- Within three months Zei was promoted to a top Arctic commander. [c31-b34]  
- Zei explains the Arctic ideology values pure competence over personal alignment, treating people as interchangeable talent. [c31-b36‑c31-b38]  
- Bai expresses admiration that Zei “played the game better than any of the others.” [c31-b39]  
- Mu asks about the most interesting Arctic advances; Zei cites medical tech that can extend life by a decade. [c31-b40‑c31-b42]  
- Zei describes Glasscrown as an ice‑crystal city with a kilometer‑high tower, underground caverns, genetically engineered pine trees, and reflective walls that warm the environment. [c31-b42‑c31-b45]  
- Zei wants the Arctic’s super‑virus research shut down, fearing its monopoly on life‑extending technology. [c31-b46‑c31-b48]  
- She argues that captured Arctic tech should be open‑sourced to benefit all humanity. [c31-b49‑c31-b52]  
- Mu reports that the Arctic garrison in Redshire has tripled and recent sabotage attempts are failing. [c31-b55‑c31-b58]  
- Deluin, citing Tafindel, proposes a hard‑ball deal: close Thaldur’s borders, let Arctic loyalists return, let Redshire defectors leave, keep Thaldur, and relocate Redshire to a new Veridian site. [c31-b60‑c31-b64]  
- The group pauses, watching snow fall on Northglade’s buildings. [c31-b64]  
- The scene shifts to Greater Plum Harbor where Gladias and Seila enter through smashed gates; security guards adopt a minimal‑intervention stance. [c31-b66‑c31-b68]  
- Seila receives a Message‑Time from Jahn showing celebratory images from Freetown and a factory bearing the Ichara defense‑company logo. [c31-b68‑c31-b71]  
- Lily runs to Gladias, embracing him; Febric, Hreda, and others join, expressing relief and familial forgiveness. [c31-b77‑c31-b83]  
- Hreda praises Greater Plum Harbor’s organized education, entertainment, and Arctic‑supplied drone food deliveries. [c31-b87]  
- Febric notes Arctic synthetic foods that mimic any taste while providing custom nutrition. [c31-b88]  
- Seila quietly acknowledges that some Arctic methods have practical benefits. [c31-b89]  
- Gladias suggests inviting new friends to share authentic Dzego cuisine, prompting excitement from Lily, Febric and Hreda. [c31-b90‑c31-b93]  
- He mentions a military funeral for Den at the mountain top before the evening meal. [c31-b93‑c31-b94]

32.text:
- The chapter follows Gladias and Seila walking through Kalimar in Meldan, Veridia on Rainmoon 12, 3725. [c32-b1] [c32-b2]  
- They see a man climb a ladder on a tree, unscrew a security camera and toss it into a box where it clangs against dozens of other cameras. [c32-b3]  
- Passing a store that recently swapped emergency rations for red Northglade liberation flowers, they read an advertisement promoting Hydrafill water seized from the Arctic Empire’s Core Territory. [c32-b4] [c32-b5] [c32-b6]  
- The path leads over a sky bridge, through a tunnel and a Y‑shaped intersection before reaching the large circular parliament building, which Gladias navigates using his watch despite never having walked there before. [c32-b7] [c32-b8] [c32-b9] [c32-b10]  
- Inside, Verdow and Zei are seated; they greet Gladias and Seila warmly and invite them to sit. [c32-b11] [c32-b12] [c32-b13] [c32-b14]  
- A robot enters; Gladias utters “dia jie fe kai ja cu dze kai lin pan,” which the robot acknowledges and exits. [c32-b15] [c32-b16] [c32-b17]  
- Verdow asks for the phrase’s meaning; Gladias translates it as “vegetable and rice,” prompting Verdow’s amused comment. [c32-b18] [c32-b20] [c32-b21] [c32-b22]  
- Verdow inquires about switching from meters to “lightfeet”; Zei explains the Bansunpei project will upgrade Dzego’s privacy standards in ten days, but immediate adoption is not a priority. [c32-b23] [c32-b24] [c32-b25] [c32-b26]  
- Verdow declares the Arctic Empire’s defeat and Northglade’s liberation, yet warns this is only the first round and the Arctics still hold Redshire and are rapidly gaining new technologies. [c32-b28] [c32-b29] [c32-b30]  
- He warns that physical privacy is leaky despite strong cybersecurity, noting new Dzego cameras with hard transmission limits are arriving for inspection. [c32-b31] [c32-b32] [c32-b33] [c32-b34] [c32-b35]  
- Gladias changes the subject, asking Verdow’s view of their government; Verdow says transparent institutions have broken and future governance will become more private, digital‑first, and sealed. [c32-b36] [c32-b37] [c32-b38] [c32-b39]  
- He identifies a fundamental tension: a government must be accountable to citizens while also pressured by powerful financial interests and external adversaries. [c32-b40]  
- Verdow suggests future mechanisms such as Silverchat polls, higher‑bandwidth communication, and AI assistance to align societal goals. [c32-b41]  
- Zei replies that AI is only the start of the conversation, raising questions about training, instruction, and oversight. [c32-b42] [c32-b43]  
- Zei observes that Veridian institutions lack predictive capacity, focusing on present public opinion rather than future outcomes. [c32-b45] [c32-b46]  
- He proposes open AI competition where AIs are players, not the game, and are held accountable to collective goals. [c32-b47] [c32-b48]  
- Verdow notes the Arctic Empire excels at unified, single‑minded goal execution, implying a “perfect goal‑executing machine.” [c32-b50] [c32-b51]  
- Zei counters that aggregating diverse goals prevents domination, but wonders whether crystallizing desires into fixed goals is inherently flawed. [c32-b52] [c32-b53] [c32-b54] [c32-b55]  
- Using a lake metaphor, Zei describes decentralized balance: water flows freely, ice forms in winter, both necessary for stability. [c32-b56] [c32-b57] [c32-b58]  
- Seila adds that the Arctics understand competition but lack cooperation, while Veridia needs both; she cites Dzego as a model that combines the two. [c32-b69]  
- Verdow invites Zei to stay and help solve these systemic issues; Zei considers the offer. [c32-b72] [c32-b73]  
- Gladias mentions Mu and Su can handle the Kungaupei and that Fin may be even more helpful. [c32-b74] [c32-b75]  
- Verdow explains Parliament recognizes its ideas have hit limits, many senators have resigned, and they are open to new input. [c32-b76]  
- He shows a world map of ninety million people, speculates on scaling to nine hundred million or nine trillion bots, and links larger populations to faster technological invention. [c32-b78] [c32-b80] [c32-b81] [c32-b82]  
- Zei worries AI will soon outpace humans, making human labor non‑restrictive; Verdow replies they lack power if the Arctics stay ahead. [c32-b83] [c32-b84] [c32-b85]  
- Verdow stresses the need to penetrate Arctic society, learn their advances, and use allies from Thaldur, mentioning Deluin as a potential informant. [c32-b86]  
- Zei cites a game‑theory result: partial mind‑reading between cooperating‑competing players can raise cooperation levels. [c32-b87]  
- Verdow warns the Arctic Emperor is scheming for a next round, possibly years away, and that keeping technological pace is essential for survival. [c32-b88] [c32-b89] [c32-b90]  
- Zei doubts slowing the Arctics; he notes mutual pressure will drive both sides forward. [c32-b91] [c32-b92]  
- Verdow envisions future tech: micro‑drones, engineered life, human uploading, and massive distributed immune systems protecting the planet. [c32-b93] [c32-b94]  
- Seila expresses hope for peace and cautions against rushed decisions about genetic engineering, uploading, or star colonization, emphasizing respect for divergent choices. [c32-b95]  
- Verdow concludes with cautious optimism, ready for any outcome. [c32-b97]  
- A robot delivers Gladias’s tea and food; Verdow invites the group to the roof, and they ascend together. [c32-b100] [c32-b101] [c32-b102] [c32-b103] [c32-b104]  
- From the roof they view Meldan’s mixed medieval‑futurist architecture, Greater Plum Harbor, the concert venue, the forest‑like Kalimar district with Silverchat headquarters, and the imposing mountain‑side castle‑tower apartments. [c32-b105] [c32-b106] [c32-b107] [c32-b108]  
- Verdow remarks on Meldan’s green versus Northglade’s snow and affirms Meldan as his home. [c32-b109] [c32-b110] [c32-b111]

script.opening: This is a summary of Snowmoon by Vitalik Buterin. It was written by AI models, not by the author: Claude, made by Anthropic, wrote it from the book and from chapter notes by gpt-oss-120b. It is read by an AI voice. It gives away the whole story, including the ending.

paragraphs.text: The story begins in Meldan, the capital of Veridia. It is a green city, full of trees, where the houses look medieval but spotless. Gladias is walking through the forest paths of the Kalimar district. His watch checks a passing drone before he can even think about it. An AI called Emerald talks quietly in his ear. In Veridia, almost nothing is banned. Instead, a decentralized body linked to the government, the Order of Steering, sets taxes that gently nudge people and businesses toward what society wants. Keepers vote on the tax rules. Sentinels audit businesses against them. Gladias is an Acolyte, an Order member in training.

But the crowd is dancing, not hating anyone. Lately the Sentinels have been pushing for a softer, gentler society. Gladias is scored on how well his votes predict theirs. His score is ninety two. paragraphs.text: The second storyline is in Dzego, a country that lost a war to the Arctic Empire a century ago. Two students, Fin and Zei, walk through Pafogai Du, a city of small electronics shops and tiny factories. Dzego's strategy has a slogan: grow roots, no head. Build everything in small, spread-out workshops. Coordinate in secret, through cryptography, with no leaders the enemy can target. Zei is a gifted student who plays a strategy game called Minpentai.

paragraphs.text: Their school keeps changing rooms at the last minute, for safety. In physics class, Zei explains entropy so well that the teacher praises him. Then a bomb goes off. The wall comes down, and a stone breaks Zei's arm. Moving rooms had saved their lives. Zei understands that the Arctic Empire is not just a lesson in geography class. It is real. Afterwards the teacher explains the Arctics' goal: to keep Dzego weak forever. Fin and Zei answer with the old saying: Dzego will rise again.

paragraphs.text: Delwart praises Gladias for his brave vote on Dreadknot. Then he makes his case. Steering is too much. It nudges everyone, and lets prejudice raise people's taxes. He wants actual freedom. His request is simple. Soon Gladias must choose to become a Sentinel or a Keeper. Choose Keeper, Delwart says, and vote to delete every rule you see. Gladias asks whether Veridia's funding, which helps Dzego defend itself, isn't important. Delwart answers that Veridia is too close to funding a war, and should focus on its own problems first. He adds that if he can find Gladias, so can others. He can protect him.

paragraphs.text: They refuse to talk to each other. The other team splits them apart, and Zei sees he cannot win alone. So he sends a ship deep into enemy territory and speaks for the first time: "Bai, next intervention turn is your chance to shine." The ship forms Bai's symbol, and together they win. Afterwards, an older friend of Zei's named Mu explains the hidden rule. The teams were not random. The game was a test of whether rivals could cooperate. They passed. Bai says sorry. Zei says she can make it up to him by taking him to Redshire one day. And his mom.

paragraphs.text: The rule for the final is new. Each player gets an AI helper, and each can read the other AI's thoughts. Bai uses this to set a trap, and Zei walks into it. He falls far behind. Then he has an idea. He builds a single factory that can carry out sixteen different attacks. Which one it fires depends on a glider that only he knows about. Bai cannot defend against all sixteen at once. Zei wins. Mu explains what the priests wanted to teach. In real life, it is not enough to think well. You must also hide your thoughts, sometimes even from your allies. In the prize bag, Zei finds a dark purple letter: for Zei's eyes only.

paragraphs.text: In Veridia, the Arctic ambassador, Lord Ephelion, debates a university president in a live broadcast. She says a society is more than its wealth: health, happiness, friendship. Ephelion answers that those things go in circles, while only growth keeps building on itself. Gladias thinks him a gifted demagogue. Then comes Gladias's own test: twenty senators must approve him. One senator, Papli, calls him out of touch. Another, Ancus, defends him. The vote is ten to ten, and the chairman breaks the tie. Gladias is in. But on the same day, Lily fails a civics test and sobs on Vil's couch. And Mov is picked at random to become a Herald, a retired member who explains the Order to the public. He has no power any more, but more time to help.

Gladias notices the argument sounds just like Delwart. Another Keeper, Eighteen, says open technology is a lifeline for Dzego.

paragraphs.text: Zei goes to Sadzu Du, Dzego's capital, for the national championship. Bai is sent there too, by Den's people, to study every player. paragraphs.text: In Veridia, Gladias tells Delwart that almost half the new Keepers share his ideas. Gladias secretly fears an Arctic attack on Redshire, but he says it probably won't happen. Delwart tells him to convince the others not to worry. Then Mov calls. He has heard Delwart through a booth wall, coaching another Keeper on the same rule as Gladias, but in a different group. The groups are kept apart so that their members think independently. Delwart has reached into two of them. This is more organized than they thought.

paragraphs.text: In the capital, Bai has been watching every game and making friends with the players. She learned those social skills, she says, to survive growing up. Her advice to Zei: the others are all too impatient. Don't rush. In the semi final, Zei is outgunned. He hides his last ship, builds another, hunkers down and outlasts his opponent. Deluin wins the other semi final the same way, by patient defense. Over tea, Deluin invites Zei to Redshire for his parents' birthdays. Zei can't afford it. Deluin shows him pictures of castles, pine forests, red snowy mountains. When I win the final, Deluin jokes, I'll use my prize money to pay for your trip.

paragraphs.text: A week later, the news breaks. The Arctic Empire has invaded and annexed Redshire. Drones and aircraft landed across the country, and an army came out of tunnels no one knew existed. Redshire's army was caught unprepared, and many suspect corruption at the top. The planes carrying the president, the prime minister and most of parliament were shot down. The president's son, Tafindel, is believed to be a prisoner. The Arctics cut Redshire off from the world.

paragraphs.text: In Dzego, Zei sits in a hotel restaurant, crying, sending message after message to Deluin. At last an answer comes. Deluin is alive, but trapped. Messages are getting out of Redshire hidden inside an Arctic soldier's health data. Zei sends back better ways to hide them, from Den's textbooks. The final is cancelled, and Zei is named champion. He does not want to win like this. Den tells him the time for hiding is over. The shadow society must become the society. The shadow government must become the government. He sends Zei back to Pafogai Du, where Dzego's secret cryptography is run.

paragraphs.text: Gladias confronts Delwart. Delwart apologizes. He was wrong about defense, he says. Then he confesses: he and a group of others work for Silverchat, the friendlier of Veridia's two big social networks. They wanted Silverchat to be a refuge from the blandness spreading through Veridia. Gladias's anger softens a little. Delwart now suggests something new: go to Dzego, learn how they deal with the Arctics, and bring it home. Mov likes the idea. Seila does not. You're not the best person for that trip, she tells him, and the Keepers need a strong hand. But if Mov agrees, go, and do your homework first. She will introduce him to Zei and Bai.

paragraphs.text: Gladias does his homework. Senator Verdow, who questioned him at his hearing, urges him to go. When Gladias mentions Zei, Verdow is delighted: Dzego's Minpentai players are so good, he would almost trust them over Dzego's army. A steward of Graph Funding, Veridia's public funding system, explains why its choices are made by random secret committees. The Arctics have just attacked the other funding system, which works by public donations. Then the vote comes. Since Redshire fell, the Keepers who wanted to drop the military tax break have gone quiet. Gladias votes no to that, and yes to raising the tax brackets, so that openness pays even more.

paragraphs.text: Gladias flies to Dzego. Zei and Bai meet him in a black car with fake windows. Pafogai Du has changed. Most shops are shut. Nearly everyone speaks through neck bands. Cars swap cabins in tunnels, so no one can follow who is inside. Then Fin arrives, after half a month away, with an answer to a question he has wondered about for years. Why does Dzego put so much effort into its language? Because Dzegoban is coordination training. When Redshire fell, the Bansunpei paused the new version of the language. Through the same channel, they sent out new privacy and security habits instead. Within three days, a new trend was sweeping all of Dzego. The Arctics believe only a strong leader can do that. Dzego does it with no head.

paragraphs.text: Zei is about to introduce Gladias to Den when a strange message arrives. Someone has paid to send it to everyone who ate at one food court in the capital. It leads to a huge hidden file. The file asks a question: what did you do on the tenth of Firemoon? That was the day of Zei's tea with Deluin, at that very food court. Zei describes it in detail, and the file opens. It is a letter from Deluin. The Arctics have taken every device in Redshire. Deluin's parents always leaned toward the Arctics, and now they are joining them. The family is flying into the Arctic Empire's heartland. Deluin does not share their views. But he will play along and win the Arctics' trust, hoping one day to help. This may be his last message. It ends: Dzego will rise again. Your dear friend, Deluin.

paragraphs.text: At a family dinner, Seila says only that someone has been manipulating the Order, telling each person what they want to hear. Zven blurts out: is it the Arctics? The table goes silent. Later, Seila calls Gladias. "Gladias, you idiot! Do you know what you've done?" Delwart was never from Silverchat, she says. He even planted that meeting for Mov to overhear. He is an Arctic. Ephelion and Delwart are not thinkers, she says. They are propagandists. Ephelion tries to win Veridians over. Delwart only had to make the Order weaker, so he told each person whatever would move them. The parts of Veridia he could not break were the private ones: the Order, the courts, the funding committees. Privacy is not a luxury. It is why we are still here.

paragraphs.text: Zei teaches Gladias an old children's game with piles of circles. With a secret trick and the right start, the second player always wins, because he gets to answer every move. Is the fight for Veridia like that? The Arctics moved first. They bribed, spied, and attacked. But in the fight for Veridia's institutions, Zei says, we can answer them. We want what the people we persuade actually want. The word for that is convincing. Gladias has the idea: do to the courts what Delwart did to the Order, but tell the truth. Verdow, on a call, offers the legal case. Veridia's law says the army must defend the country. In Northglade it failed. So the courts can fire its leaders, and fire parliament too if it gets in the way. It is crazy, Verdow admits. But Veridia is in a crazy time.

paragraphs.text: The next day, the Kungaupei try to rescue Tafindel, the captured son of Redshire's president. Zei leads the drones from a console like his old Minpentai seat, with Den and Mu on the line from other rooms. Tafindel steps onto a balcony. Then someone pulls him back inside, and Arctic drones open fire. The rescue drone is blown apart. Zei despairs. Mu takes over with a new plan. Fly low, through the streets. With passwords from friends in Redshire, she takes control of the streetlights and makes them flash wildly. At Den's call, Zei crashes a drone into the building. Tafindel and his assistant escape clinging to two drones, switch to a car, then a sea drone, and reach safety in Arturia. Zei feels he failed. Den tells him: welcome to real warfare. Sometimes you have to jump out of your chair. The Arctics have been humiliated. Now the Kungaupei can step forward.

The beauty of our world and our friendships is enough to fight for.

paragraphs.text: Through the night, Veridia's forces retreat slowly, laying traps. Fin and the language experts of the Bansunpei join the work, and they train attacks against the simulator. At sunrise, soldiers print the patterns on paper and stick them on the drones: colorful squiggles, and in giant letters, the word DOG. The Arctic drones cannot see the Veridian drones for what they are, and the Veridians tear through their lines. Zei remembers Den's words about jumping out of your chair. Den would be proud. The Arctics adapt, and access to the simulator is cut off. But Deluin sends one more message, with the exact weak points of his own units, and Zei passes them to Mu. The south breaks open. Northglade is retaken. Drones from the sea seize Thaldur, an island of the Arctic heartland. By late afternoon the battle is won, and Zei sleeps for the first time in fourteen longhours.

paragraphs.text: Two days later, on a snowy mountain above Northglade, Zei, Bai and Mu meet Deluin at last. He throws himself into Zei's arms. He tells his story. His parents went to Glasscrown, an Arctic city, to advise on bringing the conquered into the Empire. Deluin pretended to believe, and used his Minpentai fame to rise. The Arctics are easy to fool, he says. They value only talent, never loyalty. Say the right slogans, and they trust you. Their technology is real and amazing, but they keep it for themselves. Now that technology has been captured. Deluin wants it shared with the whole world, openly. But there is bad news. Redshire cannot be won back. Tafindel proposes a trade. The Arctics keep Redshire, Veridia keeps Thaldur, and anyone who wants to leave either place may go. A new Redshire will be built in Veridia. Deluin agrees, sadly.

paragraphs.text: They talk about how a society should be run. Verdow imagines a lake. Every drop of water moves on its own, and the lake still finds its level. But in winter, the water freezes into hard ice. That, Verdow says, is the ideal. In peacetime, flow like water, free and many-minded. In danger, come together like ice, to defend. Resist the Arctic Empire, without becoming one. Seila adds that the Arctics are ice without water. Veridia is water that does not yet know how to become ice. Dzego has learned to be both. Bai is thinking of spending a year in Thaldur, to understand the Arctics and look for a path to peace. Seila says she just hopes for peace. Then they climb to the roof. Below them lies Meldan: the forest of Kalimar, the walled Greater Plum Harbor, the aeroplane building, the castle towers on the mountain. Not as beautiful as Northglade, Verdow asks? The answer comes: I like the green here. And besides, Meldan is my home.

drafts.text:
Gladias walks the Kalimar foot‑path, the stone houses hugging the trees. A tiny drone buzzes overhead, and his watch confirms it is harmless. A boy snatches the drone, shouting “Five points for me!” while a grandmother gratefully accepts a seat. Emerald streams a briefing on airborne virus transmission as Gladias pauses to enjoy the view. He feels the city’s green beauty and remembers his job of judging human activity.  
SOURCES: c1-b1, c1-b2, c1-b3, c1-b4, c1-b5, c1-b6, c1-b7  

From the sky bridge he sees a forested mountain and tower‑shaped apartments. His watch buzzes with a vote request for Badra St #1103, a five‑storey building. He compares its 0.18 % aesthetics tax to a nearby corporate HQ’s 0.59 % rate. The system uses quadratic voting, balancing direction and strength. Gladias slides the slider right, choosing Tier 3, and feels a brief surge of pride.  
SOURCES: c1-b11, c1-b12, c1-b13, c1-b14, c1-b17, c1-b18, c1-b19, c1-b20, c1-b21, c1-b22, c1-b23, c1-b24, c1-b25, c1-b26, c1-b27, c1-b28, c1-b32, c1-b36, c1-b37  

The concert field is ringed by the sound‑proof barrier he saw earlier. Dreadknot’s lead singer belts violent lyrics, harsher than his taste but anthropologically valuable. Gladias must audit the performance against the tax rubric that grades social impact from Tier 1 to Tier 5. He judges the song violent yet sees a line between advocacy and entertainment, noting Sentinels now favor gentler society. His Acolyte score sits at ninety‑two, and a Tier 3 vote could keep his promotion path alive.  
SOURCES: c1-b45, c1-b46, c1-b48, c1-b49, c1-b51, c1-b53, c1-b54, c1-b55, c1-b56, c1-b57, c1-b58, c1-b60, c1-b61, c1-b62, c1-b63, c1-b64, c1-b66, c1-b67, c1-b68, c1-b69, c1-b70, c1-b71, c1-b72  

A shout erupts, “HEY EVERYONE, IT’S AN ORDER MEMBER!” and panic spreads. A decoy in a privacy robe draws attention, letting Gladias slip away. paragraphs.text: Gladias joins three other Keepers already present. He pulls out his watch, whispers into his neck band, and checks the room’s air. The watch shows 906 ppm carbon-dioxide and 4.4 µg/m³ fine particles. Moments later it updates to 918 ppm. The policy would add a tax of a third of a percent per year if indoor CO₂ exceeds a thousand ppm, with lower rates when filters or UVC are used. They mention the danger of super-pandemics, possibly released by the Arctics. One Keeper warns that some forces try to drain funding from open platforms so closed systems can dominate. They decide to work through Graph Funding, asking its channels to support open-source air-filter, cleaning and wastewater-scanning technology. They invite anyone with a breakthrough to share it. They note that older Keepers see the problem, while many newer ones seem inclined to ignore it. Seila sighs.

paragraphs.text: Zei ordered a fruit and vegetable juice and drank it quickly. He went down to the lobby, where Bai waved and Zei sat beside him. The semi-final announcer welcomed the round and named Zei against Gun. The new rule cut intervention resources by eighty percent and added five shrines that apply an XOR each thousand turns. Zei saw that the shrines broke mass conservation and realized the intervention turns were for steering. He set up his usual walls and gliders and deployed a steerable symbol-carrying spaceship he had designed. He positioned his ships so that after two intervention turns they would pass the shrines, turning them into an eternal glider factory. When the first intervention turn arrived, he launched gliders to turn rock into symbols and factories. A few hundred turns later Gun’s attack destroyed Zei’s symbol-carrying spaceship. Zei redirected his effort to protect his remaining ships, focusing east and south and abandoning the west. He began a five-intervention-turn quest to build another symbol-carrying ship, noting it would take four turns to construct one. By the fifth intervention turn his attack heavily damaged Gun’s north-west bases. At the eighth intervention turn he finished the new ship and programmed both ships to head west. He used the wreck of the old ship to trigger a glider storm at the northern shrine. The arena announced Zei Leimin as the winner.

history.text: On Firemoon dawn Zei ordered a fruit-vegetable juice, met Bai in the lobby, and heard the arena announcer declare the semi-finals. A new rule cut intervention-turn resources by eighty percent and added five XOR-shrines, breaking the usual balance. Zei studied the rule and planned a symbol-carrying spaceship that could spawn eternal glider factories after two intervention turns. In the match Zei launched his first glider storm, but Gun’s aggressive ships outpaced him, destroying a symbol-carrying ship and forcing Zei into a defensive posture. He sacrificed the western sector, concentrated attacks east and south, and built a new ship that required four intervention turns. By the fifth turn his hidden factory damaged Gun’s north-west bases, and after a frantic series of turns Zei finally completed his new ship, issued a final command and watched the arena declare him the semi-final winner.

paragraphs.text: Across United Cities a restaurant broadcast announced the Arctic Empire’s invasion of Redshire. Jahn passed through the Economics Institute turnstile, avoided the morning news, and watched a special report that described drone swarms, underground tunnels and Redshire’s swift surrender. Utaku sat beside him, typed frantically on her hand device, and looked shocked. Gladias, Seila, Febric and Hreda awoke at sunrise and saw the same news. Seila messaged Jahn. Gladias put his hand on her shoulder to comfort her. His mind soon shifted to the rubrics and tax brackets, and he recalled a recent discussion about Silverchat. He explained that the vote used a cryptographic system that hid which keys were valid, so personal presence at the Key Allocation Group was required to verify a key. Only the final result could be decrypted, preventing tampering. He flashed with anger toward Delwart.

paragraphs.text: Gladias pulled open the booth barrier and sat across from Delwart. Delwart told him he had a lot of explaining to do. He admitted his hatred of government intervention had blinded him, though that was not his main grievance. He said he worked for the covert group Silverchat, formed because its members were angry at rubrics that raised taxes after crude jokes spread on their platform. Silverchat wanted a refuge for groups like Hydrafill and Dreadknot and tried to steer Veridian politics by appealing directly to the Keepers. He warned that suppressing “blandness” could let the Arctic Empire take Redshire and later the whole world, making the effort ruinous. Gladias felt his anger mix with sympathy. A robot slid up with a salad, a rectangular nutrition bar and water, and they ate in silence before speaking again. Gladias asked what he should do now. Delwart said not to exclude the military from the rubric, that a modest tax-bracket increase would help only a tiny bit, and that the most important levers lay in Graph Funding. Later Gladias called Mov. Mov reminded him that rubric votes were in eight, twelve and sixteen days, and Delwart had suggested a trip to Dzego to learn from their experience. Gladias walked the hot, tree-lined Kalimar path and noticed a hastily taped poster advertising thirty-day survival packs. He tapped his watch and called Mov, mentioning Delwart’s confession and the Dzego suggestion. After the call he passed a restaurant, saw his uncle Febric eating, entered, removed the face cover of his privacy robe and sat beside him. A Helisport broadcast showed a purple-shirt player catch a blue ball, throw it, and knock three pins down, shifting the scoreboard. Febric praised the new scoring balance. Gladias suggested a strategy of denying opponents any point type. He asked about Lily; Febric said she had scored seventy on her civics test and was playing a secret handheld game. After they finished eating, Febric teased Gladias about zipcoins. Gladias whispered that he needed to test his social-recovery procedure and asked to buy a Hydrafill bottle. He whispered the command into his neck-band; Emerald verified the address, the amount was five and a half zipcoins, and the data field encoded Gladias’s home address, all encrypted. A security-question prompt arrived from Seila about the most unusual thing he did when the kids returned, and Gladias whispered his answer. His watch buzzed for the next signature. Mov later said Veridians, especially Keepers, needed to learn from Dzego’s experience.

history.text: In a Kalimar foot-path Gladias confronted Delwart at the same GPH booth, demanding answers. Delwart admitted his bias against government intervention and revealed he worked for the covert group Silverchat, which steered Veridian politics by influencing Keepers. He warned that suppressing blandness could let the Arctic Empire conquer Redshire and the world, and he advised modest tax-bracket tweaks, pointing to Graph Funding as the lever. Delwart also proposed that Gladias travel to Dzego to study their Arctic response and bring back insights. Gladias walked the hot, tree-lined Kalimar path, noting a poster for thirty-day survival packs, and called Mov to recount Delwart’s confession and discuss the upcoming rubric votes. Later he sat in a restaurant with his uncle Febric, removed his privacy-robe cover, and watched a Helisport broadcast where a purple-shirt player’s blue-ball throw knocked down three pins, prompting a new multiplicative scoring system. He mentioned Lily’s improved civics test and her secret handheld game, then initiated a social-recovery transaction to buy a Hydrafill bottle, whispering commands into his neck-band while Emerald verified the zipcoin address. After the meal a security-question prompt from Seila about an unusual act during the kids’ return led him to call her and announce the possible Dzego trip; Seila doubted his suitability, urged strong Keeper guidance, and pressed him to consult Graph Funding or parliamentary contacts before deciding.
history.why: written in pass 2, then shortened 2 time(s)

A robot delivered a salad, a nutrition bar and water, and they ate in silence before speaking again. Gladias asked what he should do now. Delwart said not to exclude the military from the rubric, that a modest tax-bracket increase would help only a little, and that the most important levers lay in Graph Funding. He then suggested Gladias travel to Dzego to learn how they handled the Arctic threat. Gladias walked the hot, tree-lined Kalimar path, noting a hastily taped poster advertising thirty-day survival packs. He tapped his watch and called Mov. He told Mov about Delwart’s confession, the Silverchat connection and the Dzego suggestion. Mov reminded him that rubric votes were in eight, twelve and sixteen days. Later Gladias passed a restaurant, saw his uncle Febric eating, and went inside. He removed the face cover of his privacy robe and sat beside Febric. A Helisport broadcast showed a purple-shirt player catch a blue ball, throw it, and knock three pins down, causing the scoreboard to adjust. Febric praised the new scoring balance. Gladias suggested a strategy of denying opponents any point type. He asked about Lily, and Febric said she had scored seventy on her civics test and was playing a secret handheld game. After they finished eating, Febric teased Gladias about zipcoins. Gladias whispered that he needed to test his social-recovery procedure and asked to buy a Hydrafill bottle. He whispered the command into his neck-band. The transaction address was verified by Emerald, the amount was 5.5 zipcoins, and the data field encoded Gladias’s home address, all encrypted. Febric confirmed the purchase. A security-question prompt arrived from Seila about the most unusual thing he did when the kids returned. Gladias whispered his answer, which noted he had unplugged a screen during a speech. His watch buzzed for the next signature. Later Seila called “I’m home!” and asked why he might go to Dzego. Gladias said Mov thought Veridians, especially Keepers, needed to learn from Dzego’s experience.

He explains that after the Redshire attack the Bansunpei met, put version nine on hold, and repurposed the same machinery to coordinate new changes across Dzego. He adds that the group runs A/B tests, gathers public feedback, and gives bonuses for recruiting newcomers. The conversation shifts to the Arctics’ focus on Intelligence Scores. Fin notes that the Dzegojan perspective values a community-wide Coordination Score, a collective ability to choose positive-sum cooperation. He quotes the Dzegojan motto, “grow roots, no head.”

history.text: In the hotel lobby, Bai shows Gladias a screen with a Veridian poem and a handful of Dzegoban roots. Gladias jokes he knows only two percent of the language, while Bai admits five roots. paragraphs.text: Seila’s watch flashes a red alarm: “ARCTIC EMPIRE INVADES NORTHGLADE.” A man in a privacy robe appears at her door. He authenticates with a neck-band and a green-circle scan, then leads her down to the basement. There he criticizes Veridian politicians and notes how the Keepers are split into three isolated groups. He tells her that Delwart met with someone from Silverchat and even admitted working for that group, and that this division hampers any coordinated response. Mov warns her not to use a personal copter. They hail a taxi, tap their watches on the green circle and approve the payment cryptographically. The taxi takes them to a new apartment building, and they follow a man into apartment five hundred fifteen. Inside they meet Keeper Telroy, who confirms Delwart’s anti-war stance and his opposition to tax breaks for open-source military hardware.

paragraphs.text: Seila thanks her guests for coming and keeping her company. She asks if there is any news about Febric and Hreda. She says she has sent them more zipcoins and hired a former math teacher for informal lessons. She doubts the Arctic reunify plan, fearing it could become an invasion of Veridia. Later, in the basement, she waits for Gladias’s call and hits her palm in frustration. Her watch buzzes; it is Gladias. He tells her he misses her. She feels angry and wants to scream. She shouts, “Gladias, you idiot!” She then describes the evidence. One Keeper on data-retention was told not to push privacy. Another Keeper on education was told to remove incentives for civics teaching. A third Keeper on social-media openness was left untouched. She notes that Delwart faked the Silverchat cover. She cites the preponderance of evidence and declares Delwart an Arctic operative. She lists his goals. He wants to cut open-source defense hardware. He wants unrestricted surveillance. He wants to undermine Veridian civics education. He wants to avoid social-media openness. She reminds Gladias that privacy is why they still survive. Gladias apologizes and says he loves her.

history.text: Seila welcomed her guests to a modest dinner in Veridia. She thanked them for staying, asked about the refugees’ safety, and said she had sent zipcoins and hired a former math teacher for informal lessons. She voiced doubt about the Arctic reunify plan, fearing an invasion of Veridia, and the table fell silent as the worry settled. Later in the basement she waited for Gladias’s call, accused him of being duped by Delwart’s fake Silverchat envoy, and laid out evidence of data-retention interference, rubric sabotage and the fake conversation that hid Delwart’s Arctic agenda. Gladias admitted Mov had been misled and listed Delwart’s goals of open surveillance, weakened civics and weakened defense. Together they vowed to use Seila’s Dzegojan experience to push Veridian and Dzegian parliaments toward joint resistance.

paragraphs.text: Jahn rode in a taxi, watching Freetown’s chaotic mix of glass, steel, concrete and stone. He saw advertisements for underground shelters, with luxury units priced at 325 000 zipcoins and common ones starting at 50 000. He noticed road construction increasing, especially on the northern side, even though the streets were quieter. The driver told him taxes and tolls were being raised to fund defense. After a short walk he met Utaku. Utaku mentioned a proposed unified defense grid but warned it might be more theater than substance. He said insurance premiums had tripled after the Redshire annexation, doubled again after Northglade, then fell by a quarter when defense packages were announced. He praised Dzego’s rapid rollout of privacy measures, bio-safety rules and a sharp drop in indoor carbon-dioxide levels. Their conversation turned to co-governance, where each city gives a share of its parliamentary votes to neighboring cities, and to a subsidy program that lets people swap homes and citizenships. He noted that Freetown’s constitution limits government regulation and taxation, emphasizing market-based freedom.

He noted insurance premiums had spiked after the Redshire annexation then fell when defense packages were announced, praised Dzego’s rapid adoption of privacy, bio-safety and indoor CO₂ standards, and they discussed co-governance where votes are shared among neighboring cities and the market based freedom that fuels Freetown.

history.text: Jahn rode a taxi, watching the city’s mix of glass, steel, concrete and stone pass by. Bright ads flashed for underground shelters—luxury units at 325,000 zipcoins and common ones starting at 50,000 zipcoins. He saw new road construction building up, especially on the northern side, even though traffic was lighter. The driver told him taxes and tolls were being raised to fund defense. After a short walk he ran into Utaku. Utaku spoke of a proposed unified defense grid but warned it might be more theater than substance. He mentioned that insurance premiums had surged after the Redshire annexation, rose again after Northglade, then fell when defense packages were announced. He praised Dzego’s rapid rollout of privacy measures, bio-safety rules and lower indoor CO₂ levels. paragraphs.text: Deep inside the mountain pyramid cafeteria, Gladias, Bai and Fin were seated in a private corner surrounded by shrubs and cicada-sound speakers. Zei entered, exhausted, and joined them. He said they had been ambushed by Arctic drones but managed to destroy the drones’ data-extraction chips within five minutes before the next swarm arrived. He added that the Freetown forces were very excited and that early successes could give the Kungaupei quick wins to warm them up to broader cooperation. Zei warned that scaling the effort would require confronting Veridian institutions, which would be a far tougher hurdle. He noted that Seila would try to find a solution and that Verdow was the only senator he trusted. The group then discussed a Dzegoban passage, moving from material-world small thinking to internet minimalism and its roots. They reviewed the Order of Steering’s random-selection system for tax rubrics, the Sentinels’ business audits, and the courts’ five-judge panels with penalty rules for bad-faith appeals.

paragraphs.text: Seila screamed, “Do you know what happened to Lily?” She entered Lily’s room and saw her typing on a hand device. Lily was in a chat group sharing Arctic propaganda, cheering Lord Ephelion and hoping the Arctics would come to Veridia. paragraphs.text: Gladias lay awake in the south-end pyramid after his call with Seila. He tried to sleep twice and gave up. He called his son Zven, who answered immediately. Zven said Lily’s icon had turned green, meaning she had logged in from a new device. Gladias told Zven to stay in touch with Lily, to be sympathetic and to try to learn where she was. He left the hotel area, walked through the tunnels, and noted it was his eighth day living entirely underground. He saw more biomedical, chip and automotive firms had moved into the pyramid, and the number of air filters and ultraviolet lamps had risen more than tenfold. He passed the cafeteria garden, where trees and shrubs gave calm, cut CO₂ and created private nooks. Inside, a new slogan about “tomorrow” gave him a brief surge of energy. Bai noticed him, walked up and gave him a gentle hug. She said Lily had spent a year absorbing Arctic propaganda, that Lord Ephelion’s sermons had made her feel valued, and that Lily had run away. Bai explained the Arctic doctrine: love is earned as a reward for merit, and equality is nonsense. She shared her own trauma as an Arctic orphan, how she learned to earn love through achievement, and said curiosity, not greed, was a better motivation. Later, Gladias and Zei reached a sealed door where a cloaked man, Den, welcomed them. Den admitted they had no perfect plan, but offered an unorthodox idea: to spy on the Arctics inside Veridia. He warned that if they were caught, trust between Veridia and Dzego would be lost and the Arctics would win. He offered detailed intel, contacts with Keepers, and suggested involving Verdow. Den explained that Veridia’s security cameras, once tightly limited, had been weakened, making backdoors possible. Den replied, “Yes?” indicating agreement.

Zei confirmed the Arctics had already breached Veridian security and the trio prepared to launch the covert operation, aware it could either reunite Gladias’s family or cement Arctic dominance.

paragraphs.text: Gladias and Zei sit at a tabletop that doubles as a screen. Four piles of circles show three, four, ten and thirteen pieces. Gladias, still a novice, taps one circle in the top-left pile for his first move. Zei answers by tapping the top circle of the bottom-right pile. Gladias then taps three circles from the bottom-left pile. Zei leaves a single circle in the bottom-right pile. Gladias clears the rest of the bottom-left pile, and Zei taps one circle in the top-right pile. Gladias empties the top-left pile; Zei removes two of the three circles in the top-right pile. Gladias sees that any further move would leave a single circle for Zei, and he admits defeat. Zei explains the hidden XOR rule. He says you take the binary XOR of the four counts; if the XOR sum is zero, the second player can always force a win. He shows that three, four, ten and thirteen give a zero XOR. When Gladias lowers the first count from three to two, the XOR becomes non-zero. Zei then lowers the thirteen-circle pile to twelve, bringing the XOR back to zero and securing the win. He adds that whenever the XOR starts at zero, the player who moves second can always return it to zero after each turn, guaranteeing victory. A non-zero start lets the first player win. He notes that such games are not uncommon; they favor the second player when the initial XOR is zero because the second player can see the opponent’s move and choose a counter-move that restores zero. Later Zei asks for the “secret sauce” and names the XOR algorithm as the simple mental-math trick. He also asks for the word that means showing someone a course of action that already serves their own interest. The answer is “convincing.” Zei then brings up the Courts, saying they can run the same influence campaign they used on the Order. Gladias taps his watch and sends a timed request to Senator Verdow. Verdow replies with a crazy idea: using the Fourteenth Ground Law to declare the military lawbreakers after the Northglade failure, allowing the Courts to dismiss them and, if needed, the Parliament. He says the plan is extreme but could work, and that other proposals have lower chances of success.

history.text: Gladias and Zei sit at a glowing tabletop, four piles of circles marked three, four, ten and thirteen. Gladias makes a first move, Zei replies, and the novice quickly sees he cannot avoid leaving a single circle for his opponent, so he concedes. Zei then explains the hidden XOR rule: a zero XOR guarantees the second player a win, and by reducing the thirteen-circle pile to twelve he restores the zero and forces victory. He calls this “convincing” – aligning actions with the opponent’s interests to secure a win.
