paragraphs.text: The four fly over Veridia in a small plane, watching a flat green landscape. A translated announcement gives the local time as seventy-four thousand and the temperature as seven degrees, and mentions the green plants outside. Zei gently corrects Gladias’s phrasing of “landscape of green plants.” They step through a gate marked by a green circle, and the gate welcomes them to Veridia. They meet Senator Verdow, who greets Gladias warmly. A voice notes they now know where Lily is. They learn Lily is in an Arctic-occupied boarding school in Northglade, and that Febric and Hreda are there too. A debate erupts between Lord Ephelion and Professor Sylka about the ethics of convincing people by showing how a choice serves their own interest. Later the team travels to Redshire to rescue President’s son Tafindel. An initial drone is shot down, so they adopt a low-altitude “fly-under-buildings” plan. Tafindel is lifted onto a drone, moved to a car, and finally transferred to a seaborne drone that reaches Arturia’s coast. Zei admits his failure and thanks Mu for the improvised plan. Gladias announces he will open a legal case against the Veridian military under the Fourteenth Ground Law, citing the Northglade failure. Judges invoke the Twenty-first Ground Law, reminding officials they must act honestly and without undue influence.

history.text: The trio flies over Veridia on a cold Frostime morning, lands at a bus gate that greets them with a green circle, and rides into the city where Verdow tells Gladias that Lily is held in the Arctic-occupied Northglade school. A heated debate erupts between Lord Ephelion and Professor Sylka over the Empire’s new “voluntary” recruitment clinics. Later Zei leads a daring rescue of President’s son Tafindel in Redshire; an initial drone strike is shot down, but Mu improvises a low-altitude “fly-under-buildings” tactic that confuses Arctic drones and enables Tafindel’s escape by drone, car and finally a seaborne drone to Arturia’s coast. Zei admits personal failure but praises Mu’s outside-the-box thinking. Gladias then files a legal case against the Veridian military under the Fourteenth Ground Law, arguing the Northglade failure, but Judges Caeron, Sewlert and Zevin invoke the Twenty-first Ground Law, reject immediate action and warn of parliamentary corruption, showing the limits of rapid reform.

paragraphs.text: Seila walks into Gladias’s hotel room. Gladias immediately apologizes, saying the rescue plan will not work. Seila admits she feels she has failed their family. She notes they now know where Febric, Hreda and Lily are, but see no way to rescue them unless the Arctics conquer Veridia. After a brief hug she smiles and says she has a new idea. She proposes making the judges act democratically by launching a massive Silverchat poll. The poll would need hundreds of thousands of zipcoins; Seila estimates nine hundred thousand, but their savings are only half that. She suggests convincing Evelor, the founder of Silverchat, to fund it, since the company can reclaim the fee. The three walk to the green-circle hill, enter the hidden entrance and meet Evelor. He offers tea, and after they sit he listens to Seila’s plan. She wants a poll with about a thousand questions, most decoys, and a few targeting military leadership. She initially asks for three million zipcoins; Evelor counters that one million is enough. He warns that a poll alone cannot prove the change will work. Their discussion moves to cryptographic safeguards: prediction markets, a two-party computation sandbox, and verifiable garbled circuits. Evelor notes the overhead for linear AI computation. A robot brings tea, they chant a short ritual, and the poll launches. Early results show thirty-nine percent of respondents have no confidence in the Veridian military. When filtered to Northshore voters, support for the Kungaupei rises to fifty-two percent. Mu notes a question about transferring Northshore territory to Hydrafill and also suggests delaying the related lawsuit to avoid arousing Arctic suspicion. The executive summary predicts a twenty-percent chance Veridia keeps its territory, rising to twenty-six percent under Kungaupei control and up to fifty percent if the transition is minimally disruptive. The team agrees the data are enough to strengthen Gladias’s legal case.

paragraphs.text: Zei and Mu stand on a snowy hill, cold wind blowing through the pine trees. Mu says, “So this is where our future will be decided.” He answers, “No…nothing meaningful ever happens when people are ready.” Footsteps echo behind them, and Bai catches up and hugs Zei from behind. She says, “Whatever happens today, Zei, I am happy that I got to know you.” Zei pulls her up to his level and replies, “I am happy that I got to know you too.” The three stand in silence, watching snow drift over the trees to their east. Mu asks, “So what’s the plan?” He tells them they will strike tonight, push into the northern part of Northshore from the west, bypass Northglade and then surround it.

Mu then outlines the strike: move west into Northshore, bypass Northglade and surround it.

paragraphs.text: Inside a cramped war room Den, Mu, Zei and dozens of generals listen to Lektor’s briefing. Lektor assigns the northern front to Gallowar, the central front to Telpo, the southern front to Den and the naval front to Vakaria, then tasks Zei with supervising all fronts. The map on the screen matches the plan they have just heard. Lektor dismisses everyone, giving three long hours to prepare before a sundown launch.

paragraphs.text: Back on the hill, thousands of snow-mobile-like drones sit at the forest edge, their backs fitted with thin silver fiber-optic cables. The cables will let Zei stay in contact with the drones as the front moves forward. Bai points out a box of printers perched on one drone. Mu says other drones carry paper, shirts and classroom gear for rapid visual attacks on Arctic algorithms. Zei’s watch buzzes, counting one hundred ticks until sunset, recalling the Minpentai games that trained him. Mu whispers, “Time to get back to our command post.” Zei turns; the sun is already halfway below the horizon. He replies, “Indeed, we should.”

paragraphs.text: When the clock struck midnight, the three land groups surged forward while the naval launch was held back. An alarm blared. Gallowar shouted that they were adopting defensive positions, and Telpo ordered part of Group Center northward for a flanking attack. “For Veridia!” rang out, and Lektor called, “Alright everyone.” Zei directed the drones to use the Redshire tactics, aware the Arctic AI would adapt quickly. Emerald scanned the micro-tactical fields and reported that only tactics one and five had any effect. Zei ordered all units to drop the other tactics and concentrate on one and five. A message then arrived from Deluin, who identified himself as an Arctic commander and described a weakness he had set on the southern front.

Land groups advance quickly while the naval launch is delayed, and an alarm sounds at Northglade as Gallowar and Telpo coordinate defensive and flanking moves. Lektor rallies the troops, shouting for Veridia as the battle intensifies. Zei deploys tactics learned in Redshire, but the Arctic AI adapts, reducing their effectiveness. Emerald’s analysis shows only a few tactics work, prompting Zei to reorder them. A urgent message from Deluin arrives, revealing he is an Arctic commander who has planted a weakness on the southern front.

paragraphs.text: Zei watches the battle from the command screen, after earlier urging a slow retreat that Lektor has adopted. Deluin’s reply arrives with proxy endpoints for safe queries. Fin evaluates the offer almost instantly and says it is doable. Emerald creates a real-time chat for the team. They set up printing stations about two kilometres behind the front and paste paper patterns onto the snow drones. The patterns more than double the AI’s detection time. The Veridian drones achieve casualty ratios better than ten to one, but later the Arctic forces form defensive circles and the ratio falls to about six to one. Deluin then sends southern-front coordinates; Zei forwards them to Mu, who hands control of the southern fleet to Vakaria. Vakaria’s drones sweep north and link up with Telpo after a long hour.

history.text: On Snowmoon thirty Zei spends the night commanding the drone battle and coordinating retreats. Lektor implements Zei’s slow-retreat strategy while Deluin sends encrypted offers of proxy endpoints for safe queries. Fin quickly evaluates the proposal and Emerald creates a real-time chat group for collaborative hacking. The team prints paper patterns, applies them to drones and sees detection time rise, improving casualty ratios before Arctic forces form defensive circles. Mu receives southern-front orders, hands control to Vakaria and the southern fleet sweeps north, linking with Telpo after a long hour.

paragraphs.text: Zei, Bai and Mu climb a snow-covered mountain staircase that a maintenance drone keeps clear. At the summit they reach a circular platform with a full view of Northglade. From the east they see the main city; to the west and north the hills stretch endless. A young man in a sweater and hood appears on the opposite stairs and throws himself into Zei’s arms for a hug, asking if he knows them. He greets Mu with a laugh. Zei then tells the story of the Arctic occupation of Redshire, how his parents went from peace-seeking to ardent supporters, and how the Arctics offered them positions in Glasscrown. He explains he pretended to side with the Arctics, using his Minpentai champion status to rise, and within three months became a top commander. He describes Glasscrown as an ice-crystal city with a kilometer-high tower and deep underground caverns. He says he would shut down the Arctic super-virus research. Mu asks what the most interesting Arctic advances are. The group pauses, watching snow fall over the town.

Hreda says the district runs organized schools, entertainment and even gets food delivered by Arctic drones. paragraphs.text: Gladias and Seila walk along the road. They see a man climb a ladder against a tree, unscrew a security camera and fling it into a box of dozens of others, the clang echoing. They pass a store whose shelves now hold red Northglade liberation flowers, and a taped advertisement for Hydrafill water seized from the Arctic Empire’s Core Territory. Their path crosses a sky bridge, then a tunnel, and a Y-shaped intersection. It ends at a large circular building. Gladias taps his watch and the doors open. Inside, Verdow and Zei greet them warmly and invite them to sit. A robot slides into the room. Gladias speaks a clear phrase to it; the robot buzzes and leaves. Verdow declares that the Arctic Empire has been defeated and Northglade is free. He warns that this was only the first round. The Arctics still hold Redshire and are rapidly gaining new technologies. He says future government will become more private, digital-first, with sealed rooms and AI assistance. He mentions using Silverchat polls and higher-bandwidth communication to understand people’s goals. Zei replies that Veridian institutions lack predictive capacity. He proposes an open AI competition where AIs are players, not masters. The group follows Verdow to the roof. From there they see Meldan’s mixed medieval-futurist architecture, the grey and purple Greater Plum Harbor, and the forest-like Kalimar district with the Silverchat headquarters. They also see towering castle-style apartment buildings on the mountain. Verdow comments on Meldan’s green versus Northglade’s snow and says Meldan is his home.

history.text: Gladias and Seila walk through Kalimar, passing a man who climbs a ladder on a tree, unscrews a security camera and tosses it into a box of dozens of others. They see a store that swapped emergency rations for Northglade liberation flowers and an advertisement promoting Hydrafill water seized from the Arctic Empire’s Core Territory. Their path leads over a sky bridge, through a tunnel and a Y-shaped intersection to the large circular parliament building, which Gladias navigates using his watch despite never having walked there before. Inside, Verdow and Zei greet them warmly; a robot enters, acknowledges a phrase Gladias speaks, then leaves. Verdow declares the Arctic Empire’s defeat and Northglade’s liberation, yet warns the fight is only beginning and the Arctics still hold Redshire and are gaining new technologies. He outlines a future of transparent, digital-first institutions with AI assistance and Silverchat polls, while Zei counters that Veridian institutions lack predictive capacity and proposes open AI competition where AIs are players, not masters. The group ascends to the roof, viewing Meldan’s mixed medieval-futurist architecture, Greater Plum Harbor, the forest-like Kalimar district with Silverchat headquarters, and the imposing mountain-side castle-tower apartments. Verdow remarks on Meldan’s green versus Northglade’s snow and affirms Meldan as his home.

+ Zei and Bai tap their hand devices at the glowing green turnstiles and walk onto the single spiral floor.

+ Bai leans in and asks about Zei’s arm, and Zei confirms it was broken when his classroom was bombed.

- Seila’s watch pings with a message from Gladias, showing his face.
- Gladias asks how her time in Freetown is, and she replies they had lunch with “lovely kids from Dzego.” He mentions someone suggested he become a Keeper instead of a Sentinel.
- Gladias thinks the Keeper role can set rubrics correctly and seems more interesting.
- Seila encourages the idea, noting that Graph Funding helps Dzego but current rubrics do not reward helpful products, and she suggests making rubric adjustments a Keeper project.
+ Seila taps her watch and sees Gladias’s face on the screen.
+ Gladias asks how her time in Freetown is.
+ She answers that they just had lunch with lovely kids from Dzego.
+ He then says someone suggested he become a Keeper instead of a Sentinel.
+ Gladias believes the Keeper role will let him set the rubrics correctly and will be more interesting.
+ Seila says she supports the idea.
+ She notes that Dzego benefits from Graph Funding, but the current rubrics do not reward helpful products.
+ She suggests that adjusting the rubrics could be a Keeper project.

- Back in Veridia, Gladias dons his privacy robe, neck band and watch, and calls Mov for technical help.
- He asks Mov to confirm the basement’s anti-transmission foil is secure before submitting his Keeper track decision.
- Mov warns him about Delwart’s movements and suggests watching the mysterious gentleman at GPH tea shops.

- He heads to the assembly, noting the violet UVC lights, fans, and the discussion on public-space rubrics.

+ He asks Mov to verify that the basement’s anti-transmission foil is still secure before he files his Keeper track decision.
+ Mov reminds him to watch Delwart, noting that the mysterious gentleman has been moving from one tea shop to another, and urges Gladias to keep his eyes open.
+ Gladias then takes out a reputation-backed loan using a zero-knowledge proof.
+ He heads to the citizens’ assembly, noticing the faint violet UVC lights, the ceiling fans, and the lively discussion about public-space rubrics.

- Gladias walks through a sky bridge, a tunnel, and a massive outdoor staircase toward a tower where ten Order members await.
- The members activate a glowing green circle that scans his cryptographic nullifier “three-seven-two-eff.” The system confirms his identity and his choice to apply for Keeper status.

+ Gladias walks across a sky bridge, through a tunnel, and up a massive outdoor staircase that leads to a tower where ten Order members stand waiting.
+ He steps before a glowing green circle, taps his watch, and the circle flashes green, verifying his cryptographic nullifier “three-seven-two-eff.” He declares, “I am applying to become a Keeper,” and the system replies with a confirmation.
+ The brief ceremony thus marks his official entry onto the Keeper track.

- In Pafogai Du, Zei faces Bai in the final Minpentai match, each equipped with personal AIs.
- The AIs share full read access to each other’s thought transcripts, turning the duel into a meta-strategic battle.
- Zei builds a hidden symbol-carrying spaceship that exploits a blind spot in Bai’s AI, which ignores diagonal attacks.
- He floods the board with diagonal gliders and a factory-triggered spaceship, overwhelming Bai’s defenses.
- The audience erupts as the score swings to a 14-to-11 lead for Zei, and Bai eventually resigns at 12-to-6.
+ In Pafogai Du, Zei meets Bai in the final Minpentai match.
+ Both players have personal AIs, and the AIs can read each other’s thought transcripts, making the duel a meta-strategic contest.
+ Zei asks his AI to set up his usual glider and wall patterns, and he also builds a hidden symbol-carrying spaceship by hand, a structure the AI does not reveal to Bai.
+ Scanning Bai’s transcript, Zei discovers that her AI pays no attention to attacks coming down the diagonals.
+ He responds by sending a wave of diagonal gliders and by ordering a factory that will activate when a glider arrives from the southwest.
+ The factory creates a set of sixteen strategies, stretching Bai’s AI to its limits.
+ The pressure forces Bai’s defenses to falter, and the score climbs to fourteen to eleven as the crowd cheers.
+ Later the board reads twelve to six, and Bai resigns, ending the match.

- Mu congratulates both players and explains that the rule allowing AIs to read each other mirrors the opaque yet trustworthy Veridian Steering system.
- He notes the lesson that success depends on clever thinking and on concealing one’s own thoughts, even from allies.
- Zei receives a cryptographic token kit, hoping it will finally let him buy a new compute box for his mother.
- Bai examines her gifts, while Zei immediately scans his code, confirming his personal motivation.
- Later, a robot delivers a dark-purple envelope addressed “For Zei’s eyes only,” hinting at a secret reward.
+ Mu congratulates both players and notes the Veridian Steering system as an opaque yet trustworthy part of government.
+ He adds that success requires clever thinking and also hiding one’s thoughts, even from allies.
+ Zei receives a cryptographic token kit and scratches open its code, hoping it will finally let him buy a new compute box for his mother.
+ Bai examines her gifts, while Zei scans the code, still driven by that goal.
+ After Mu leaves, Zei discovers a dark-purple envelope marked “For Zei’s eyes only” and puts it in his pocket.

- Gladias boards a bus, watches passengers glued to hand devices, and sees a live VNU debate between Professor Sylka and Lord Ephelion.
- Sylka argues that health and social bonds matter more than gross economic output, invoking the Steering mechanisms.
- Ephelion counters that long-term success still correlates with high economic output, calling growth the “largest eigenvector.” At the parliamentary hearing, Gladias answers rapid-fire questions, mentions his Colorball childhood, and defends open platforms for Dzego’s people.

+ Gladias boards the autobus and steps inside.
+ He notices many passengers glued to their hand devices.
+ He looks at a passenger’s screen and sees a live VNU debate between Professor Sylka and Lord Ephelion.
+ Sylka says that focusing only on gross economic output limits progress and stresses citizens’ health, emotional well-being and social bonds, pointing to the Steering mechanisms.
+ Ephelion replies that long-term success still follows high economic output.
+ He calls growth the “largest eigenvector” that drives lasting improvement.
+ In the parliamentary hearing, Gladias answers rapid-fire questions, mentions playing Colorball as a child, and says he hopes to support Dzego’s people.
+ The vote ends in a ten-to-ten tie.
+ The Chairman casts the deciding “Yes,” and Gladias is welcomed into the Order of Steering.

- After the hearing, Gladias’s watch buzzes with a call from Mov, who reveals he has become a Herald.
- Mov explains he lost formal power but will help Gladias, confirming the “cryptographic random gods” selection system.
- Gladias immediately calls Seila, shares his narrow acceptance, and hears her enthusiastic congratulations.
- Seila expresses confidence that Gladias will reshape rubrics as a Keeper.
- He prepares to pursue Keeper projects with Seila’s support.
+ Later that evening, Gladias receives a call from Mov.
+ Mov tells him he has been chosen by the cryptographic random gods to become a Herald, losing his formal power but gaining more time to help Gladias.
+ Gladias then phones Seila.
+ He shares that he barely got into the Order, and Seila celebrates, saying she knew he would and that she’s excited for the good he can do as a Keeper.
+ He promises to try his best.

- Bai and Fin sit together in a courtyard, sharing food while Bai weeps.
- Fin tries to comfort her, saying Zei is a nice kid who could help them if they were nicer.
- Bai snaps, demanding to know what “nicer” means, and shouts “NO!” when Fin mentions her mother.
- She tells Fin her parents died in a lab explosion and that she knows who caused it.
+ Bai and Fin sit in a courtyard, eating and drinking while tears run down Bai’s face.
+ Fin tells her that Zei is a nice kid and that if she were nicer to him he could help them.
+ Bai, distressed, asks “Nicer, like you?” Fin hesitates, then recalls the time Zei brought his mother on the trip to Freetown.
+ He adds a hint, saying he felt the same after the recent game when Bai suggested he bring his own mother along, and Bai shouts “NO!” Fin then asks if she dislikes her mother.
+ Bai snaps, saying Fin has never asked who her mother is in any of their meetings.
+ She reveals that both her mother and father died in a lab explosion when she was a child and that she knows who caused it.
+ Fin’s expression drops.

- Fin pulls out a thin booklet titled “po so dze go ban de sia.” He explains that Dzegoban aims for easy learning, logical syntax, pleasant speech and real-world usefulness.
- He notes the language moved from pictorial script to alphabet after the war, shedding complex grammar.
- He points out the separators “li” and “fe” that mark subject-verb-object, making sentences machine-parseable.
- Bai smiles, promising to study its history on her own.
+ Fin pulls out a thin booklet titled “po so dze go ban de sia.” He says Dzegoban is meant to be easy to learn, logical in its syntax, pleasant to speak, and useful for real-world topics.
+ He explains that the grammar uses the separators “li” and “fe” to mark subject-verb-object, so a program can parse a sentence unambiguously.
+ He adds that brackets “lo” and “zo” let speakers build more complex phrases, though some ambiguity can remain.
+ He notes the Bansunpei priests try to keep meaning regular even if perfect consistency is impossible, and that knowing the 256 roots lets speakers understand most everyday speech.

- The scene shifts to a mountain pyramid where Zei follows his watch’s directions to a sealed green door.
- Inside, a cloaked priest named Den greets him, identifying himself as a High-Council member of the Kungaupei.
- Den tells Zei the Kungaupei is a secret defense society that builds a shadow army for Dzego.
- He praises Zei’s recent Minpentai performance and asks about his cryptography knowledge.
+ Zei follows his watch through the winding tunnels of the mountain pyramid, checking each fork as he goes.
+ The watch leads him to a sealed door marked by a green circle, which he taps and watches open slowly.
+ Inside he finds a narrow, long chamber ending in a large table where a cloaked figure sits.
+ The man introduces himself as Den, a High Council member of the Kungaupei.
+ Den explains that the Kungaupei is a secret defense society that builds a shadow army for Dzego.
+ He tells Zei he has studied the recent Minpentai game and is impressed by the strategy Zei displayed.

- Den explains modern cryptography has moved beyond factoring because of Arctic quantum threats.
- He describes obfuscation protocols that hide program internals and offers Zei a place in the Kungaupei.
- Zei’s broken left arm twitches, a reminder of his recent injury.
- Den proposes Zei continue the Minpentai nationals, study cryptography, and take future tasks.
+ Den says modern cryptography has moved beyond factoring because the Arctic quantum threat makes those methods obsolete.
+ He explains obfuscation protocols that let a program run without revealing its internals, describing how meta-program tricks can hide code.
+ He tells Zei he wants to recruit him into the defense effort.
+ He urges Zei to keep competing in the Minpentai nationals, to study cryptography, and promises to suggest future tasks.

- Zei agrees to join, and Den leads him to a black car whose doors match the pyramid’s seal.
- The car rides through a hidden tunnel, keeping Zei’s location secret.
- They arrive at a room filled with empty white boxes and an automated chip-packing line.
- Den shows a diagram of a three-layer mixnet that hides sender identity, then demonstrates how physical goods can be delivered through it.
- Zei sees a microscope-filled inspection facility where multi-wavelength 3-D scanning verifies chips.
+ Zei agrees, and Den takes him to a black car.
+ The car’s door opens onto a staircase that drops into a basement, shielding them from view.
+ They walk down and enter a large room filled with thousands of empty white boxes and a machine that automatically places chips into the boxes.
+ Den pulls up a diagram on his hand device and explains a mixnet: each message is wrapped in three layers of encryption, passes through three randomly chosen nodes, and finally reaches its destination, the payload still encrypted.
+ He points out that the sealed boxes and their bar-coded labels act as the physical mixnet, letting chips be delivered without anyone knowing which package is inspected.
+ After the tour, Den taps his watch, a green-outlined circle glows and a door opens.
+ They move through a hallway, turn a corner and step into a chamber dominated by a large microscope.
+ There, Den shows a system that scans chips with multiple wavelengths of three-dimensional light to confirm they match the exact specifications.

- In Freetown, Gladias meets Utaku, a doctorate student from Belpaki, at a restaurant table.
- Utaku mentions the “Arctic scare” and rising defense budgets in neighboring regions.
- She explains that megacorps now donate three percent of revenue to defense and punish non-contributors, citing Mogna’s forced exit.
- Gladias listens, aware the Arctic threat looms over Veridia.
+ In Freetown, Jahn sits at a restaurant table with Utaku, a doctorate student from Belpaki.
+ She brings up the Arctic scare, noting that only Redshire and its neighboring regions are taking it seriously.
+ Utaku explains that megacorps now donate three percent of their revenue to defense and collude to punish those who refuse.
+ She cites Mogna, which was forced out after the charging-station network threatened to lock its cars out unless it contributed.
+ Jahn listens.

- Later Gladias enters a privacy booth for the first Keeper meeting on cultural values.
- The Keepers debate Dreadknot’s tax increase, fearing over-taxing artists will dull Veridia’s culture.
- Gladias argues for balance, noting the rubric pushes blandness.
- The group then moves to a second booth to discuss the hardware-openness rubric, debating whether military products should be exempt.
- He worries about mentioning Delwart, fearing Seila’s bias toward Dzego.
+ Gladias steps into a privacy booth for a Keeper meeting on cultural values.
+ Inside, the Keepers review the cultural-values rubric and question Dreadknot’s recent tax increase on content.
+ They worry that heavy taxes could make artists’ work boring and pale.
+ Gladias notes that the rubric itself pushes blandness and calls for a more balanced approach.
+ After that, they move to a second booth to discuss the hardware-openness rubric, debating whether military and surveillance products should be exempt.
+ While speaking, Gladias hesitates about mentioning Delwart, aware that Seila may favor positions that benefit Dzego.

- During the second meeting a hidden spying device is discovered under the table.
- Keeper Eighteen destroys the bug, then the group resumes the openness discussion.
- Zero argues that exempting military hardware undermines societal benefit, suggesting higher steering taxes instead.
- Another Keeper counters that strong defense preserves independence in the mountainous United Cities.
- The Keepers agree to reflect individually, noting the final vote is six months away.
+ During the second meeting a hidden spying device is found under the table.
+ Keeper Eighteen destroys the bug, then the group returns to the openness rubric.
+ One Keeper says the chaos of the game tree means they should raise steering taxes on all military hardware.
+ Another Keeper points out that strong defense lets the United Cities keep their independence in the mountains.
+ The Keepers agree to think about it on their own, noting the final vote is six months away.

- Den and Mu appear after Zei’s semi-final loss in the Minpentai nationals.
- They praise his cryptography work and reveal that Minpentai is covert military training.
- Den warns Zei that secrecy is vital, lest he expose the program.
- Zei promises to keep the Kungaupei’s agenda hidden, even from Fin, and accepts the hidden purpose.
+ Zei steps into the long room and sees Den and Mu waiting.
+ They commend his rapid progress in cryptography and his perfect test scores.
+ They tell him that Minpentai is military training.
+ Den warns that if Zei reveals what he has learned, the program could be exposed.
+ Zei replies that he will not tell anyone, not even Fin, and agrees to keep working on the cryptography tasks and the nationals.
+ The two nod, thank him, and finish with a quiet Veridian phrase.

- At a school field in Meldan, Gladias watches his son Zven play the Helisport game.
- Four bright red ball-shaped drones launch from a ramp, and children chase them in yellow and purple shirts.
- Zven catches a red ball, collides with another copter, then grabs a fourth ball to secure the win for his team.
- Gladias notes the AI-assisted rotor control that makes the drones so responsive.
+ At a school field, Gladias watches his son Zven’s first Helisport game.
+ A large truck sits in the centre of the grass.
+ An instructor opens a small box and four bright red ball-shaped drones spring out.
+ Children in yellow and purple shirts strap into personal copters and chase the drones.
+ Zven spots a red ball, flies toward it and catches it, earning the first point for the yellow team.
+ He later catches another ball, bringing the sixth point and the win for his team.
+ Gladias remarks that the AI on the drones is getting very good.

- After the game Gladias enters a Keeper booth for the air-quality policy.
- He records indoor CO₂ at nine hundred six ppm and PM2.5 at four point four, questioning the high CO₂ despite functional filters.
- The Keepers debate raising the indoor-air-quality tax from a third to two-thirds of a percent of land value, citing pandemic risk from the Arctics.
- They also discuss funding, criticizing the current Quadratic Funding round as corrupted by a Bluewhale whistle-blower scheme.
- Gladias doubts the efficacy of Graph Funding and private-school rubrics.
+ After the Helisport game, Gladias steps into a Keeper booth.
+ He finds three other Keepers already waiting.
+ He pulls out his watch, whispers into his neck band, and checks the room’s air.
+ The display shows carbon-dioxide at about nine hundred parts per million and fine-particle levels low; a moment later it updates to just over nine hundred.
+ The policy they are reviewing would add a tax of a third of a percent per year if indoor carbon-dioxide climbs above a thousand, with lower rates if filters or UVC are used.
+ The Keepers mention the danger of super-pandemics, possibly released by the Arctic region.
+ One Keeper warns that some forces try to drain funding from open platforms so closed systems can dominate.
+ The group decides to work through Graph Funding, asking its channels to support open-source air-filter, cleaning and wastewater-scanning technology, and invites anyone with a breakthrough to share it.
+ They note that older Keepers see the problem, while many newer ones seem inclined to ignore it, and Seila sighs.

- Zei arrives by train at Sadzu Du for the national Minpentai championship.
- He checks in at hotel 304, showers, and reads a cryptography textbook on hash functions during the ride.
- The ceremony opens with Taskmaster Jin announcing the schedule and tie-breaking formula.
- In the fourth qualifying match Zei experiments with east-moving gliders, discovers a time-reverse cheat, and finally sends a glider backwards to create symbols.
- He attacks opponent Bo’s base, destroys all three of Bo’s symbols, and is declared the winner of the fourth qualifying match.
+ Zei faces Bo in a match.
+ The crowd watches closely, with Bai, Fin, Mu and Den among the onlookers.
+ Spectators are surprised, noting that neither contestant has found any gliders that move up or down.
+ Just before the third intervention turn, one of Zei’s gliders strikes a rock formation beside Bo’s home base, giving Zei a clear view of Bo’s three symbols.
+ He uses that turn to launch gliders toward each of the symbols and some nearby spots.
+ Within three hundred turns all three symbols are gone, and the announcer declares Zei the winner.

- Gladias entered the quiet GPH booth on a Harvestmoon morning and found Delwart already seated.
- He told Delwart that the first-year Keepers were demanding fewer interventions and lighter rubrics.
- Delwart replied that the Keepers were making their case more convincingly than Gladias ever could.
- Gladias admitted he feared sabotage but worried Delwart would lecture him if he doubted it.
+ Gladias entered the booth on Harvestmoon 8 and saw Delwart already seated.
+ He told Delwart that many first-year Keepers want fewer interventions and lighter rubrics.
+ Delwart replied that the Keepers were making their case better than Gladias ever could.
+ Gladias admitted he feared a sabotage campaign but worried Delwart would lecture him if he voiced that doubt.

- Seila asked Hreda about a math exam, and Hreda’s high score made Seila worry about Lily’s performance.
- Lily watched a Helisport broadcast until it suddenly cut to a propaganda video from Lord Ephelion, the Arctic Empire consul, denouncing Veridia’s egalitarian doctrine.
- Seila lunged to unplug the screen, but Lily, absorbed in her handheld device, finished her meal without reacting.
- The family left the restaurant uneasy, aware that the Empire’s messages were reaching their home.
+ Seila asked Hreda how the math exam went, and Hreda’s ninety-six percent score made Seila worry for Lily.
+ Lily stared at the table while the robot served the meals, and the family watched a Helisport broadcast.
+ The game suddenly cut out and was replaced by a propaganda video featuring Lord Ephelion of the Arctic Empire denouncing Veridia’s egalitarian doctrine.
+ Seila tried to unplug the screen.
+ Lily kept tapping her handheld device, later her face lit up, she cheered, put the device down and finished her food before anyone else.
+ The family ate in silence as the broadcast continued.

- The next day Gladias returned to the booth where a secret Keepers group gathered behind anonymized neck-bands.
- Keeper Zero proposed amending the hardware-openness rubric to tax all military, surveillance and counter-surveillance products at a minimum Tier three.
- Keeper Eighteen warned that the Arctic Empire’s technological edge made any delay dangerous, while Delwart downplayed the threat.
- Gladias suggested postponing the vote for two months, letting any Arctic sabotage decide the outcome.
- The group accepted his compromise, buying time for the looming decision.
+ Gladias slipped back into the booth where the other Keepers were already assembled.
+ A proposal was put forward to amend the hardware-openness rubric, making all military, surveillance and counter-surveillance products subject to a minimum Tier 3 tax.
+ Eighteen warned that the Arctic Empire’s technological advantage made the threat asymmetric.
+ Delwart replied that the Arctics were unlikely to launch attacks.
+ Gladias then suggested waiting two months and letting any Arctic sabotage decide whether the amendment should pass.
+ The group accepted the compromise and agreed to revisit the vote later.

- On Firemoon dawn Zei ordered a fruit-vegetable juice, met Bai in the lobby, and heard the arena announcer declare the semi-finals.
- A new rule cut intervention-turn resources by eighty percent and added five XOR-shrines, breaking the usual balance.
- Zei studied the rule and planned a symbol-carrying spaceship that could spawn eternal glider factories after two intervention turns.
- In the match Zei launched his first glider storm, but Gun’s aggressive ships outpaced him, destroying a symbol-carrying ship and forcing Zei into a defensive posture.
- He sacrificed the western sector, concentrated attacks east and south, and built a new ship that required four intervention turns.
- By the fifth turn his hidden factory damaged Gun’s north-west bases, and after a frantic series of turns Zei finally completed his new ship, issued a final command and watched the arena declare him the semi-final winner.
+ At dawn on Firemoon Zei ordered a fruit-vegetable juice, went down to the lobby and met Bai.
+ The arena announcer then welcomed the semi-finals and named Zei versus Gun.
+ A new rule cut intervention-turn resources by eighty percent and added five shrines that apply an XOR each thousand turns.
+ Zei read the rule, saw that the shrines broke mass conservation, and decided to use his steerable symbol-carrying spaceship.
+ He positioned it so that after two intervention turns it could create an eternal glider factory.
+ He began the match by sending gliders, but Gun’s ships moved faster and destroyed one of Zei’s symbol-carrying ships.
+ Zei gave up the western sector, focused his attacks east and south, and started a five-intervention-turn effort to build another ship, knowing each symbol-carrying ship needs four turns to construct.
+ By the fifth intervention turn his hidden factory damaged Gun’s north-west bases.
+ After many turns he finished the new ship, sent both ships west, and the arena announced Zei Leimin as the winner.

- In the waiting room Zei watched the final between Deluin and Kau.
- After the match a robot greeted them with a strange phrase and a menu appeared, startling Zei.
- Deluin complimented Zei’s style, and they discussed the new Dzegoban symbols being A slash B tested.
- Deluin offered to fund a Redshire visit within fifteen days, but Zei declined, citing a lack of money.
+ In the waiting room Zei watched the match between Deluin and Kau.
+ After the game a robot slid to their table, spoke a strange phrase, and a menu appeared, making Zei gasp.
+ Deluin asked Zei about his game and Zei remarked his style was uglier than Deluin’s.
+ They talked about the new Dzegoban symbols that were being A/B tested.
+ Deluin invited Zei to visit Redshire, saying he could pay and joking it might happen in fifteen days.
+ Zei said he didn’t have the money.

- Across United Cities a restaurant broadcast announced the Arctic Empire’s sudden invasion of Redshire.
- Jahn walked through the Economics Institute turnstile, avoided the morning news, then watched a special report detailing drone swarms, underground tunnels and the swift surrender of Redshire.
- Utaku, seated beside him, typed furiously, eyes wide with alarm.
- Meanwhile in Meldan Gladias, Seila, Febric and Hreda awoke to the same shocking news at sunrise, and Seila messaged Jahn to confirm his safety.
- Gladias comforted Seila, then turned his mind to the looming Keeper vote.
- He discussed the invasion’s impact with Mov, noting Delwart’s recent Silverchat meetings and the failure of Delwart’s political predictions.
- Gladias explained that the upcoming vote used a cryptographic system that hid which keys were valid, making individual verification impossible without personal presence at the Key Allocation Group.
- He left angry at Delwart but determined to protect Veridia’s institutions.
+ Across United Cities a restaurant broadcast announced the Arctic Empire’s invasion of Redshire.
+ Jahn passed through the Economics Institute turnstile, avoided the morning news, and watched a special report describing drone swarms, underground tunnels and Redshire’s swift surrender.
+ Utaku sat beside him, typed frantically and looked shocked.
+ In Meldan, Gladias, Seila, Febric and Hreda awoke at sunrise and saw the same news.
+ Seila messaged Jahn.
+ Gladias put a hand on her shoulder to comfort her, then his thoughts turned to the upcoming Keeper vote.
+ He recalled Delwart’s recent Silverchat meetings.
+ Gladias explained that the vote used a cryptographic system that hid which keys were valid, so individual verification required personal presence at the Key Allocation Group.
+ He left angry at Delwart.

- In a Kalimar foot-path Gladias confronted Delwart at the same GPH booth, demanding answers.
- Delwart admitted his bias against government intervention and revealed he worked for the covert group Silverchat, which steered Veridian politics by influencing Keepers.
- He warned that suppressing blandness could let the Arctic Empire conquer Redshire and the world, and he advised modest tax-bracket tweaks, pointing to Graph Funding as the lever.
- Delwart also proposed that Gladias travel to Dzego to study their Arctic response and bring back insights.
- Gladias walked the hot, tree-lined Kalimar path, noting a poster for thirty-day survival packs, and called Mov to recount Delwart’s confession and discuss the upcoming rubric votes.
- Later he sat in a restaurant with his uncle Febric, removed his privacy-robe cover, and watched a Helisport broadcast where a purple-shirt player’s blue-ball throw knocked down three pins, prompting a new multiplicative scoring system.
- He mentioned Lily’s improved civics test and her secret handheld game, then initiated a social-recovery transaction to buy a Hydrafill bottle, whispering commands into his neck-band while Emerald verified the zipcoin address.
- After the meal a security-question prompt from Seila about an unusual act during the kids’ return led him to call her and announce the possible Dzego trip; Seila doubted his suitability, urged strong Keeper guidance, and pressed him to consult Graph Funding or parliamentary contacts before deciding.
+ Gladias pulled open the booth barrier and sat across from Delwart.
+ He demanded answers.
+ Delwart admitted his hatred of government intervention had blinded him, but said it was not his main grievance.
+ He revealed he worked for the covert group Silverchat, which formed because its members were angry at rubrics that raised taxes after crude jokes spread on their platform.
+ Silverchat wanted a refuge for groups like Hydrafill and Dreadknot and tried to steer Veridian politics by appealing directly to the Keepers.
+ Delwart warned that if they suppressed “blandness” the Arctic Empire could take Redshire and later the whole world, making their effort ruinous.
+ Gladias felt his anger mix with sympathy.
+ A robot delivered a salad, a nutrition bar and water, and they ate in silence before speaking again.
+ Gladias asked what he should do now.
+ Delwart said not to exclude the military from the rubric, that a modest tax-bracket increase would help only a little, and that the most important levers lay in Graph Funding.
+ He then suggested Gladias travel to Dzego to learn how they handled the Arctic threat.
+ Gladias walked the hot, tree-lined Kalimar path, noting a hastily taped poster advertising thirty-day survival packs.
+ He tapped his watch and called Mov.
+ He told Mov about Delwart’s confession, the Silverchat connection and the Dzego suggestion.
+ Mov reminded him that rubric votes were in eight, twelve and sixteen days.
+ Later Gladias passed a restaurant, saw his uncle Febric eating, and went inside.
+ He removed the face cover of his privacy robe and sat beside Febric.
+ A Helisport broadcast showed a purple-shirt player catch a blue ball, throw it, and knock three pins down, causing the scoreboard to adjust.
+ Febric praised the new scoring balance.
+ Gladias suggested a strategy of denying opponents any point type.
+ He asked about Lily, and Febric said she had scored seventy on her civics test and was playing a secret handheld game.
+ After they finished eating, Febric teased Gladias about zipcoins.
+ Gladias whispered that he needed to test his social-recovery procedure and asked to buy a Hydrafill bottle.
+ He whispered the command into his neck-band.
+ The transaction address was verified by Emerald, the amount was 5.5 zipcoins, and the data field encoded Gladias’s home address, all encrypted.
+ Febric confirmed the purchase.
+ A security-question prompt arrived from Seila about the most unusual thing he did when the kids returned.
+ Gladias whispered his answer, which noted he had unplugged a screen during a speech.
+ His watch buzzed for the next signature.
+ Later Seila called “I’m home!” and asked why he might go to Dzego.

- Jahn rode a taxi through United Cities on Mistime twenty-two.

- Gladias lay awake in the south end pyramid haunted by the call with Seila.

- Later Den greeted Gladias and Zei behind a sealed door, proposing a risky spy project to expose Arctic infiltration within Veridia.
- Zei confirmed the Arctics had already breached Veridian security and the trio prepared to launch the covert operation, aware it could either reunite Gladias’s family or cement Arctic dominance.

+ He passed the cafeteria garden, where trees and shrubs gave calm, cut CO₂ and created private nooks.
+ Inside, a new slogan about “tomorrow” gave him a brief surge of energy.
+ Bai noticed him, walked over and gave him a gentle hug.
+ She told him Lily had spent a year absorbing Arctic propaganda, that Lord Ephelion’s sermons had made her feel valued, and that Lily had run away.

+ Later, Gladias and Zei reached a sealed door where a cloaked man, Den, welcomed them.

+ He warned that if they were caught trust between Veridia and Dzego would be lost and the Arctics would win.

+ Zei noted that Veridia’s security cameras, once tightly limited, had been weakened, making backdoors possible, and confirmed the Arctics had already infiltrated Veridia.

- Gladias and Zei sit at a glowing tabletop, four piles of circles marked three, four, ten and thirteen.
- Gladias makes a first move, Zei replies, and the novice quickly sees he cannot avoid leaving a single circle for his opponent, so he concedes.
- Zei then explains the hidden XOR rule: a zero XOR guarantees the second player a win, and by reducing the thirteen-circle pile to twelve he restores the zero and forces victory.
- He calls this “convincing” – aligning actions with the opponent’s interests to secure a win.
- Inspired, Gladias activates his watch, calls Senator Verdow and outlines a plan to expose Arctic backdoors, invoke the Fourteenth Ground Law and empower the courts to dismiss the military and Parliament if needed.
- Verdow proposes a bold legal move and a covert campaign to sway judges before the Arctic Empire can react, giving Gladias a surge of hope.
+ Gladias and Zei sit at a tabletop that serves as a screen, with four piles of circles showing 3, 4, 10 and 13.

+ He admits defeat.
+ Zei then explains the hidden XOR rule: when the XOR sum of the pile counts is zero, the second player can always force a win.
+ He shows that the starting board has a zero XOR, and by reducing the thirteen-circle pile to twelve he restores the zero and secures victory.

+ Gladias taps his watch, calls Senator Verdow and proposes using the Fourteenth Ground Law to label the military as lawbreakers and let the courts dismiss them and, if needed, the parliament.

- The trio flies over Veridia on a cold Frostime morning, lands at a bus gate that greets them with a green circle, and rides into the city where Verdow tells Gladias that Lily is held in the Arctic-occupied Northglade school.

- Seila bursts into Gladias’s hotel room, apologizing for a failed rescue plan and proposing a massive Silverchat poll to force judges to act, even though it would cost nine hundred thousand zipcoins.

drafts.text:
Gladias walks a foot‑path through Kalimar, tall trees and stone houses. A small drone drifts overhead. A boy from a four‑child family snatches the drone, shouting “Five points for me!” A grandmother with a child is offered a seat by a couple, and she accepts gratefully.  
NOTES: 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5  

Emerald streams a briefing on airborne virus transmission and ventilation. Gladias whispers “Pause, I want to enjoy the view” to Emerald. From the sky bridge he sees a forested mountain. He also sees castle‑tower‑styled apartment blocks on its slope. He reflects that Veridia’s nature is beautiful and his job is to give opinions on the human world.  
NOTES: 1.6, 1.8, 1.9, 1.10  

His device buzzes with a vote request for Badra St #1103. He knows he was selected by cryptographic sortition to rate the building’s aesthetics tax. He compares Badra St’s tax rates with a nearby aeroplane‑shaped corporate HQ. He thinks the current rates seem fair but worries the aeroplane building may be over‑taxed. The system uses quadratic voting to balance direction and strength. After a pause he slides the slider slightly right and selects his vote.  
NOTES: 1.13, 1.14, 1.15, 1.16, 1.17, 1.18  

At the concert gate his device presents a cryptographic proof and lets him in. Attendees wear dark‑purple Veridian Privacy Robes. Dreadknot’s lead singer performs violent lyrics. Gladias must audit the performance against the tax rubric that grades social impact. His Acolyte prediction score is ninety‑two, keeping him on track for promotion. He chooses Tier 3, feeling a brief surge of pride.  
NOTES: 1.20, 1.21, 1.24, 1.25, 1.29, 1.31  

A shout “HEY EVERYONE, IT’S AN ORDER MEMBER!” triggers panic. A decoy in a privacy robe draws attention, giving Gladias a chance to flee. A burly man points a device at him, and Gladias distracts him with a question about the Arctic Emperor. He snatches the device, deletes recent recordings, and runs. He hops onto a nearly empty autobus, noting other privacy‑robe wearers and a teenage passenger. Inside the bus ads promote lifelong learning and Hydrafill’s sugar‑free drinks.  
NOTES: 1.32, 1.33, 1.34, 1.35, 1.36  

He returns home and greets his partner Seila. Their children argue over dinner orders, and Lily reveals a low history exam score. Seila comforts Lily. The family plans to stay with Uncle Vil for six months, hoping for freedom. A doorbell delivers food boxes, which Gladias distributes. While eating, he receives an anonymous verified message noting he was seen at the concert and that the sender will not report him but has a request.  
NOTES: 1.38, 1.39, 1.40, 1.41, 1.43  

Fin and Zei step off the autobus onto Hun Min street, a bustling commercial‑industrial avenue. To the left stand a sensor shop and an anti‑transmission foil store, symbols of Dzegojan tension. A friendly security drone flies overhead, and their watches authenticate it in milliseconds. They note the street’s neon‑lit electronics shops.  
NOTES: 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.5  

Zei internally recites “grow roots, no head,” the half‑century strategy Dzego uses to stay protected. Fin asks Zei about the Minpentai game, and Zei boasts a third‑place finish using a reflective wall structure. Zei’s watch flashes a new cryptographic proof system for class entry. They calculate they have under ten minutes, about a thousand ticks, to reach the classroom, confirming they are on schedule.  
NOTES: 2.4, 2.6, 2.9, 2.10  

The classroom walls are lined with anti‑transmission foil over cartoonish Dzego propaganda, and a poster displays DU’s motto about learning freeing individuals and nations. The instructor opens the door and announces a physics lesson on thermodynamics. He asks about entropy in information theory and the second law, but few students claim to explain the connection. Zei proposes a thought experiment about reversing mixing, invoking time‑reversible physics. Suddenly a loud crash shakes the room, part of the wall collapses, and a stone fragment injures Zei’s arm.  
NOTES: 2.12, 2.13, 2.14, 2.16, 2.18  

The instructor checks on the students and scans Zei’s arm, revealing a broken bone that needs hospital care. Fin offers to escort Zei to the hospital so he can still compete in the upcoming game. Smoke fills the room, and watches’ air‑quality monitors beep before quieting as filters clear the air. Zei jokes that they now know less about the wall than two minutes ago, lightening the mood. The instructor declares the class has had enough entropy for the day and dismisses everyone. Fin and Zei stay behind, cleaning debris while the instructor reflects on the Arctic Empire’s new focus on physics education.  
NOTES: 2.20, 2.21, 2.22, 2.23, 2.24, 2.25  

Gladias walks through Meldan’s sidewalks flanked by small shops. He passes a tunnel where a poster signed by Lord Ephelion urges Veridians to “build the future.” Mov taps Gladias on the shoulder, claiming to be the Arctic Emperor and threatening to “suck out your soul.” Mov reminds Gladias that he added him to a trust list a year ago, allowing local AIs to share location data for today’s meeting. They discuss the openness rubric and recent Bluewhale API restrictions, noting the platform closed its API to only verified hardware and is taxed at the maximum rate.  
NOTES: 3.2, 3.4, 3.6, 3.7, 3.9, 3.10  

Inside a GPH booth, a man in a privacy robe introduces himself as Delwart and claims knowledge of Gladias’s family. Delwart asks whether Gladias is satisfied with the current Steering system, and Gladias replies it feels fine despite flaws. They discuss the Dreadknot concert tiering, noting Sentinels pushed the band to Tier 4 while Gladias voted Tier 3. Delwart proposes “actual freedom” by abolishing nudges in Steering and deleting every rubric, urging Gladias to become a Keeper. Gladias counters that systemic change requires many Keepers, not just one, and worries about losing Graph Funding that supports Dzego’s defense.  
NOTES: 3.24, 3.25, 3.26, 3.28, 3.29

The president's son, [Tafindel](/təfˈɪndᵊl/), is believed to be a prisoner. The Arctics cut Redshire off from the world.

paragraphs.text: In Veridia, Gladias watches the news with Seila at sunrise. His first thought is that the Keepers will surely not cut the military tax break now. His second is anger at Delwart. He and Mov agree: Delwart owes them answers. The Order's voting system protects Gladias, at least. Only he can register his voting key, in person, with people who know him. So Delwart cannot check his votes or cast them for him.

Whatever happens today, she says, I am happy I got to know you. The plan is to strike that night. Lektor commands, with army groups to the north, center and south, and drones by sea. Den leads the southern group. Zei watches over the drone tactics on every front. He realizes that every Minpentai game he ever played was training for this night.

paragraphs.text: The first clash goes well. But then the main battle turns. Most of Zei's tricks no longer work. He realizes the Arctics must have learned from the drones he fought in Redshire. Then a message arrives: a rear base has been destroyed by Arctic missiles, probably betrayed by traitors. Den was there. He almost certainly did not survive. Zei cries. Mu takes over Den's group. Zei believes the battle is lost.

paragraphs.text: Then his watch buzzes. It is Deluin. He has won the Arctics' trust and is now one of their commanders, in charge of their southern flank. He sends tactics to break through it. But can they trust him? Bai has an idea. We have no reason to trust Deluin, she says, but he has every reason to trust us. So let him take the first leap. Ask him for the Arctic drones' AI. With it, they could design patterns that make the drones blind to them. Deluin cannot get the AI itself. But he gives them access to the Arctics' own simulator.

paragraphs.text: Through the night, Veridia's forces retreat slowly, laying traps. Fin and the language experts of the Bansunpei join the work, and they train attacks against the simulator. At sunrise, soldiers print the patterns on paper and stick them on the drones: colorful squiggles, and in giant letters, the word DOG. The Arctic drones cannot see the Veridian drones for what they are, and the Veridians tear through their lines. Zei remembers Den's words about jumping out of your chair. Den would be proud. The Arctics adapt, and access to the simulator is cut off. But Deluin sends one more message, with the exact weak points of his own units, and Zei passes them to Mu. The south breaks open. Northglade is retaken. Drones from the sea seize Thaldur, an island of the Arctic heartland. By late afternoon the battle is won, and Zei sleeps for the first time in fourteen longhours.

paragraphs.text: Two days later, on a snowy mountain above Northglade, Zei, Bai and Mu meet Deluin at last. He throws himself into Zei's arms. He tells his story. His parents went to Glasscrown, an Arctic city, to advise on bringing the conquered into the Empire. Deluin pretended to believe, and used his Minpentai fame to rise. The Arctics are easy to fool, he says. They value only talent, never loyalty. Say the right slogans, and they trust you. Their technology is real and amazing, but they keep it for themselves. Now that technology has been captured. Deluin wants it shared with the whole world, openly. But there is bad news. Redshire cannot be won back. Tafindel proposes a trade. The Arctics keep Redshire, Veridia keeps Thaldur, and anyone who wants to leave either place may go. A new Redshire will be built in Veridia. Deluin agrees, sadly.

paragraphs.text: In the Greater Plum Harbor of Northglade, the gates are smashed open. Gladias and Seila walk through, and a door opens before they can knock. Lily runs out and hugs her father. Febric and Hreda follow. Lily says sorry to her mother. Don't be, Seila tells her. We all made lots of mistakes this year. We're a family. That afternoon, they will honor Den and the fallen soldiers at a funeral on the mountain. Then their new friends from Dzego will come and cook them real Dzego food.

paragraphs.text: Back in Meldan, Gladias and Seila walk the Kalimar path where the story began. A man is unscrewing security cameras from the trees and dropping them in a box. A shop sells red flowers from Northglade. A Hydrafill ad offers fresh water seized from the Arctic heartland. At parliament, Gladias orders his meal from the robot in Dzegoban. Verdow warns that this was only the first round. The Arctics kept Redshire, and they are racing ahead in new technology. Veridia's secret institutions worked: the Order, the courts, the funding committees. Its open ones failed. Many senators have resigned, and parliament wants new ideas. He asks Zei to stay and help.

paragraphs.text: They talk about how a society should be run. Verdow imagines a lake. Every drop of water moves on its own, and the lake still finds its level. But in winter, the water freezes into hard ice. That, Verdow says, is the ideal. In peacetime, flow like water, free and many-minded. In danger, come together like ice, to defend. Resist the Arctic Empire, without becoming one. Seila adds that the Arctics are ice without water. Veridia is water that does not yet know how to become ice. Dzego has learned to be both. Bai is thinking of spending a year in Thaldur, to understand the Arctics and look for a path to peace. Seila says she just hopes for peace. Then they climb to the roof. Below them lies Meldan: the forest of Kalimar, the walled Greater Plum Harbor, the aeroplane building, the castle towers on the mountain. Not as beautiful as Northglade, Verdow asks? The answer comes: I like the green here. And besides, Meldan is my home.
